description: Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

title: Workshop in Counseling
subject: Counselor Education
description: Faculty-supervised intensive and interactive program focusing on the development of specific skills.

title: Topics
subject: Counselor Education
description: Various current topics in counseling and counseling psychology are offered. Contact the department office for information about topics courses planned for the near future.

title: Internship
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Students provide counseling services to diverse clients in either a school or community agency setting. Supervision is provided by experienced counselors in the field setting with coordination by program faculty. Attendance at a weekly seminar on campus is required. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Leadership, Advocacy and Professional Issues
subject: Counselor Education
description: Advanced course in the study of leadership, advocacy for clients/profession/communities, current professional issues, and ethics in the profession of counseling and counselor education.

title: Seminar in Counseling
subject: Counselor Education
description: Doctoral seminars in topics such as professional issues, teaching and consultation are offered for advanced graduate students.

title: Advanced Theories of Counseling and Psychotherapy
subject: Counselor Education
description: An in-depth comparison and contrast of major theories of counseling and psychotherapy. Theories representative of existential, psychoanalytic and behavioral viewpoints are considered.

title: Teaching in Counselor Education
subject: Counselor Education
description:
This course focuses on various models, perspectives, research, and techniques pertaining to learning to teach in counselor education. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Counselor Education.

title: Supervision of Counseling Services
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Includes principles and techniques involved in developing and supervising counseling and guidance services in a variety of settings, including colleges and universities, public schools and various community agencies. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Counselor Education.

title: Advanced Practicum in Counseling
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Practical experience in a public, private or non-profit organization, supervised by a professional with an academic component overseen by a UNM instructor.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Advanced Multicultural Counseling
subject: Counselor Education
description: This course will provide counselor education doctoral students with knowledge and skills to teach and conduct advanced research in multicultural counseling.

title: Consultation, Program Evaluation, and Research in Counselor Education
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Provides counselor education doctoral students the knowledge and skill to conduct professional consultation, program evaluations, and counseling research. Curriculum builds on research and writing skills, applying them to professional evaluation and writing in counselor education.
Prerequisite: EDPY 500 or (EDPY 502 and EDPY 505) or EDPY 511.
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Counselor Education.

title: Advanced Group Counseling and Psychotherapy
subject: Counselor Education
description: An advanced course in group counseling and group psychotherapy. Topics include therapeutic factors, group process observations, here-and-now work, and supervision of group work.

title: Internship
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Practical experience in a public, private or non-profit organization, supervised by a professional with an academic component overseen by a UNM instructor.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Dissertation
subject: Counselor Education
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a doctoral dissertation.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Introduction to Human Services
subject: Counselor Education
description: This course provides a broad overview of the human services field. Students will be exposed to the broader mission of the human services professions, as well as trace its development across history.

title: Introduction to Helping Skills
subject: Counselor Education
description: This course is designed to teach basic interviewing techniques used in a variety of settings. Theoretical foundations of various interviewing styles and techniques will be examined. The student will develop an awareness of ways in which the interviewer’s background, attitudes, and behaviors influence the interview.

title: Introduction to Group Dynamics
subject: Counselor Education
description: An introduction to basic issues and stages of development in the group counseling process; overview of types of counseling groups, group theory, leadership ethical guidelines, group formation and termination.

title: Life Designing and Career Development in Human Services
subject: Counselor Education
description: Provides a practical and theoretical foundation for understanding the life design paradigm. Career development theories, occupational and educational information, life balance and decision-making processes, and career and life design techniques for working in the field.

title: Forensic Science
subject: Criminal Justice
description: This course provides the non-science major with an introduction to forensic science. The course creates a basis for understanding many of the concepts and techniques on which forensic science is built.

title: Social Issues in Urban and Regional Development
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduction to the social, economic, political and physical factors involved in the development of cities and towns. Emphasis on the nature of urban form as a reflection of the prevailing past and present political economy of society.

title: Sustainable Community Planning Methods
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Teaches the basic concepts, processes and techniques of planning. Students learn to identify planning issues, problems and research questions; collect information to answer these questions; organize and analyze information; and develop policy recommendations.

title: Community Change in a Global Era
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course examines the intersections among globalization, communities, and social action. It focuses on myriad ways global forces impact communities and how they work for local change in a global era.

title: Introduction to Urban Design
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course introduces students to issues associated with the design of cities and aims to establish an understanding of the theories and methodologies of urban design.

title: Community Economics for Planners
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduces the intersections of economic theory and contemporary economic development issues and policies. Surveys how economic decisions and policies impact the shaping of space and development of communities. Introduces strategies to strengthen local economies.

title: Stakeholders and Environmental Policy
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course examines the complexity of environmental policymaking, and how stakeholders can impact and are impacted by environmental planning and policy at different scales.

title: Policing the City, From Albuquerque to Rio
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course explores the dynamics of security, policing and inequality in diverse processes of urban development. Using global comparative perspectives, it explores the uneven distribution of safety, vulnerability and violence within and across communities. The course fulfills UNM's U.S. & Global Diversity & Inclusion Requirement.

title: Community-Based Practice
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Exploration of practical skills for creating and implementing community based programs and plans with community partners. Skill development in mobilization, facilitation, and organizational development to implement community based plans and strategies.

title: Qualitative Research Methods
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of qualitative inquiry. It focuses primarily on preparing students to conduct rigorous qualitative research, community based planning and analysis.

title: Watershed Restoration Field Techniques
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Taught in the field and lab, this course focuses on various techniques used in natural resources and restoration planning. It also explores what Dr. Robin Kimmerer describes as restoration reciprocity, restoring people’s relationship to land.

title: Community Placemaking Studio
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course addresses physical planning analytical methods and presentation skills, and prepares students for professional roles as active and effective participants in the ongoing process of managing the urban spatial environment.

title: Watershed Management
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: An introduction to the watershed as a rational planning unit, with case studies to illustrate principles of resource inventory, identification of land use problems and the formulation of plans for protection and rehabilitation.

title: Problems
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Problems are individualized topics conducted on a one to one student-faculty arrangement. Allows for exploration of various subjects of interest to students and faculty members.

title: Indigenous Environmental Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course focuses on the theory and practice of environmental planning involving indigenous peoples and their lands.

title: Seminar
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Various topics related to planning in the southwest.

title: Planning on Native American Lands
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: The social, political and economic interrelations between tribal lands and their activities with the outside dominant society. Case studies are used to present views in support of tribal autonomy and tribal integration.

title: Culture, Place and Power in Community Development
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Theories of community development and democratic practice in places marked by racial, ethnic, cultural and other forms of difference, through a global comparative frame and with attention to relationships of power. Relevant to B.A.E.P.D.

title: Community Growth and Land Use Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Study of land use planning and growth management dynamics at the local level, in its physical, legal administrative and economic contexts. 
Restriction: admitted to B.A.E.P.D. Environmental Planning and Design.

title: Planning Issues in Chicano Communities
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Applies planning concepts and techniques to development issues facing Chicanos in New Mexico generally and Albuquerque specifically. Other Chicano communities are studied for the insights gained from a comparative approach.

title: Planning Theory and Process
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
A broad overview of planning theory and history, with a focus on current planning paradigms as they apply in practice. Introduces students to the roles professional planners play in practice and the strategies they employ and dilemmas they encounter. 
Restriction: admitted to M.C.R.P. Community and Regional Planning.

title: Community-Based Practice
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Exploration of practical skills for creating and implementing community based programs and plans with community partners. Skill development in mobilization, facilitation, and organizational development to implement community based plans and strategies.

title: Analytical Methods for Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduction to comparative analysis of social, economic and spatial data as integrated into a typical comprehensive plan. Building data sets, organization of information, use of survey research, preliminary forecasting methods. Descriptive statistics a prerequisite.

title: Qualitative Research Methods
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduces students to the methods and techniques of qualitative inquiry. It focuses primarily on preparing students to conduct rigorous qualitative research, community based planning and analysis.

subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Taught in the field and lab, this course focuses on various techniques used in natural resources and restoration planning. It also explores what Dr. Robin Kimmerer describes as restoration reciprocity, restoring people's relationship to land.

title: Watershed Management
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: An introduction to the watershed as a rational planning unit, with case studies to illustrate principles of resource inventory, identification of land use problems and the formulation of plans for protection and rehabilitation.

title: Internship
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Professionally based experience in professional planning practice in public, private or non-profit settings. Supervision is given in the field setting as well as at an academic setting. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Foundations of Community Development
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Explores what it takes to practice community development. What are processes of community development and how can planners enhance and build community in ways that promote fair and just distribution of resources and impacts.

title: Foundations of Natural Resources
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: A foundation for applying planning concepts and analytical techniques to natural systems in regions. Ecology and environmental policy, land suitability analysis, natural resources accounting and impact assessment.

title: Foundations of Physical Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: An introductory course of physical planning practice for Planning, Architecture and Landscape students. Graphic methods of analysis, field trips, cross-disciplinary projects range from regional plans to design details of the built environment.

title: Foundations of Indigenous Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Examines the relationship of indigenous planning to other planning approaches such as advocacy, equity, and radical planning; considers aspects of "indegeneity" such as sovereignty, land tenure, and culture, and their application to community planning.

title: Community Economics for Planners
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Explores the intersections of economics and contemporary economic development issues and policies. How do economic decisions and policies impact the shaping of space and development of communities? Covers strategies to strengthen local economies.

title: Visualization Tools for Plan Making
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course introduces students to fundamental techniques and tools used to create graphics in plan making. It is designed for planners to learn to communicate ideas graphically using both hand drawing and design software.

title: Urban Systems
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: The study of city systems, form, and development with emphasis on social, economic, political, and physical aspects of cities as partial and total systems.

title: Indigenous Environmental Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course focuses on the theory and practice of environmental planning involving indigenous peoples and their lands.

title: Transportation Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Introduction to urban transportation subject area in a seminar format. Characteristics of urban transportation systems in U.S. and foreign cities are explored as are effects of urban transportation on local economies, urban form, the environment and the neighborhood.

title: Problems
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Individual study of problems in planning undertaken with faculty advisement and supervision. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Seminar
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Various topics related to planning in the southwest.

title: Planning on Native American Lands
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: The social, political and economic interrelations between tribal lands and their activities with the outside dominant society. Case studies are used to present views in support of tribal autonomy and tribal integration.

title: Cultural Aspects of Community Development Planning
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Development theory, community planning and human ecology in different cultural settings. The course examines cases in Latin America, Southeast Asia, Western Europe and the U.S. as contexts for applied exercises. Relevant to B.A.E.P.D.

title: Development and Latin America
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course covers key theories and histories about development in Latin American contexts. The dynamics of development include the political, economic, social, spatial and epistemological dimensions of social change, operating at multiple scales.

title: The Politics of Land
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
This course engages with the politics of land and land use. It explores the legal, administrative and economic processes through which land is conceptualized, exchanged and used. 
Restriction: enrolled in M.C.R.P. program.

title: Planning Issues in Chicano Communities
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: This course applies planning concepts and techniques to development issues facing Chicanos in New Mexico generally and Albuquerque specifically. We study other Chicano communities for the insights gained from a comparative approach.

title: Political Economy of Urban Development in a Global World
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: Analyzes the political and economic factors shaping urban development with particular emphasis on the impacts of economic restructuring. As planners, we study how these changes affect the process of planning and policy formation.

title: Project Development
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Development of project or thesis concept, investigation of data needs, initial data collection and assembly of written and field materials necessary to conduct a professional project or thesis. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.  
Restriction: admitted to M.C.R.P. Community and Regional Planning.

title: Professional Project II
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Development of a professional project reflective of advanced work in the field. Project should have an identified client, a time frame and a final product which demonstrates competence to engage in professional level planning. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Historic Research Methods
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description: An introduction to the methods for the documentation, research and analysis of historic built environments as preparation for historic preservation and contemporary regional design.

title: Capstone Planning Studio
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Advanced studio projects responsive to client needs and useful to community organizations and public agencies. Results in final planning products which demonstrate competence to engage in professional level planning. Content varies each year.
Restriction: admitted to M.C.R.P. program.

title: iTown Studio
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
This is an exit studio in the M.C.R.P. program and builds on the skills acquired in the first year of CRP classes. Students are expected to produce planning document deliverables to the indigenous community.
Restriction: admitted to a graduate program in the School of Architecture and Planning.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Community & Regional Planning
description:
Development of a research project reflective of advanced inquiry into a planning topic. Thesis should make concrete contributions to guide planning practice. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Introduction to Computer Architecture and Organization
subject: Computer Science
description:
Survey of various levels of computer architecture and design: microprogramming and processor architecture, advanced assembly language programming, operating system concepts and input/output via the operating system.  
Prerequisite: 241L with a grade of "C" or better and ECE 238L with a grade of "C" or better.
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Design of Large Programs
subject: Computer Science
description: A projects course with emphasis on object-oriented analysis, design and programming. Also discussed are programming language issues, programming tools and other computer science concepts as needed to do the projects (e.g., discrete-event simulation, parsing).

title: Declarative Programming
subject: Computer Science
description: Course focuses on one of the declarative programming paradigms: functional, logic, or constraint programming. Specialized techniques are introduced with a view towards general principles. Selected advanced topics in programming language design and implementation are covered.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
subject: Computer Science
description: An introduction to data structures and algorithms and the mathematics needed to analyze their time and space complexity. Topics include asymptotic notation, recurrence relations and their solution, sorting, hash tables, basic priority queues, search trees (including at least one balanced structure) and basic graph representation and search. Students complete a term project that includes an experimental assessment of competing data structures.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms II
subject: Computer Science
description:
A continuation of 361L with an emphasis on design of algorithms. Topics include: amortized analysis and self-adjusting data structures for trees and priority queues; union-find; minimum spanning tree, shortest path and other graph algorithms; elementary computational geometry; greedy and divide-and-conquer paradigms.  
Prerequisite: 361L with a grade of "C" or better.
 Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Introduction to Numerical Computing
subject: Computer Science
description:
n introductory course covering such topics as solution of linear and nonlinear equations; interpolation and approximation of functions, including splines; techniques for approximate differentiation and integration; solution of differential equations; familiarization with existing software.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Topics in Computer Science for Non-Majors-Undergraduate
subject: Computer Science
description: This course is intended to provide students in other disciplines with an opportunity to study aspects of modern computer science, tailored to their own field of study.

title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to technical aspects of raster algorithms in computer graphics.  Foundational concepts of 2-D and 3-D graphics as relate to real-time and offline techniques.  Students develop a video game as a final project to demonstrate the algorithms learned in class.

title: Introduction to Complex Adaptive Systems
subject: Computer Science
description:
Introduces topics in complex adaptive systems, including: definitions of complexity, fractals, dynamical systems and chaos, cellular automata, artificial life, game theory, neural networks, genetic algorithms and network models. Regular programming projects are required. 
Prerequisite: 251L and MATH 1522. 
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Principles of Artificially Intelligent Machines
subject: Computer Science
description: Survey of artificial intelligence exclusive of pattern recognition. Heuristic search techniques, game playing, mechanical theorem proving, additional topics selected by the instructor.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to principles and practice of systems that improve performance through experience. Topics include statistical learning framework, supervised and unsupervised learning. Bayesian analysis, time series analysis, reinforcement learning, performance evaluation and empirical methodology; design tradeoffs.

title: Introduction to Parallel Processing
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to parallel scientific and data intensive programming architectures and systems. Performance issues, speed-up and efficiency. Parallel programming issues and models: control parallel, data parallel and data flow. Programming assignments on massively parallel machines.

title: Introduction to Cybersecurity
subject: Computer Science
description:
This class will focus on proactive security i.e. designing networks, algorithms and data structures which are probably robust to attack. Grades will be based on class participation, presentations, and class projects. 
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Compiler Construction
subject: Computer Science
description:
Syntax analysis and semantic processing for a block-structured language. Lexical analysis, symbol tables, run-time management. Students will write a compiler.  
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Advanced Declarative Programming
subject: Computer Science
description: Continued study in one of the declarative programming paradigms: functional, logic, or constraint programming. Specialized techniques are introduced with a view towards general principles.

title: Software Engineering
subject: Computer Science
description:
Software engineering principles will be discussed and applied to a large team developed project. Other topics relevant to the production of software will also be covered, including ethics, legalities, risks, copyrights and management issues.

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Database Management
subject: Computer Science
description:
Introduction to database management systems. Emphasis is on the relational data model. Topics covered include query languages, relational design theory, file structures and query optimization. Students will implement a database application using a nonprocedural query language interfaced with a host programming language.
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Principles and Applications of Big Data
subject: Computer Science
description:
This course explores data analysis and management techniques, which applied to massive datasets are the cornerstone that enable real-time decision making in distributed environments, business intelligence, and scientific discovery at large scale.
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Computational Modeling for Bioengineering
subject: Computer Science
description: An interdisciplinary study of Python programming, kinetic modeling of chemical reactions, illustrated by computational applications in bioengineering, in particular, the modeling and design of genetic regulatory networks.

title: Introduction to Scientific Computing
subject: Computer Science
description:
Parallel programming, performance evaluation. Error analysis, convergence, stability of numerical methods. Applications such as N-body problem, heat transfer, wave propagation, signal processing, Monte-Carlo simulations. C, C++, or FORTRAN skills required. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Computer Operating Systems
subject: Computer Science
description:
Fundamental principles of modern operating systems design, with emphasis on concurrency and resource management. Topics include processes, interprocess communication, semaphores, monitors, message passing, input/output device, deadlocks memory management, files system design. 

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Computer Networks
subject: Computer Science
description:
Theoretical and practical study of computer networks, including network structures and architectures. Principles of digital communications systems. Network topologies, protocols and services. TCP/IP protocol suite. Point-to-point networks; broadcast networks; local area networks; routing, error and flow control techniques.

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Special Topics-Undergraduates
subject: Computer Science
description:
Undergraduate seminars in special topics in computer science.  
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Advanced Topics in Computer Science
subject: Computer Science
description:
This course will cover advanced topics in Computer Science.
Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Individual Study-Undergraduate
subject: Computer Science
description: Guided study, under the supervision of a faculty member, of selected topics not covered in regular courses. At most 3 hours may be applied toward the CS hour requirement. Restriction: admitted to School of Engineering.

title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation
subject: Computer Science
description: Covers basic topics in automata, computability and complexity theory, including: models of computation (finite automata, Turing machines and RAMs); regular sets and expressions; recursive, r.e., and non-r.e. sets and their basic closure properties; complexity classes; determinism vs. non-determinism with and without resource bounds; reductions and completeness; practice with NP- and P-completeness proofs; and the complexity of optimization and approximation problems.

title: Computational Geometry
subject: Computer Science
description: Development of algorithms and data structures for the manipulation of discrete geometric objects in two- and three-dimensional space. Typical problems include intersection and union of polyhedra, convex hulls, triangulation, point location, neighborhood structures and path computations.

title: Mobile Computing
subject: Computer Science
description: Internet and wireless communication are two technologies having a significant impact on the social fabric. This course is concerned with methods and principles for the development of systems that exhibit some form of mobility.

title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
subject: Computer Science
description: Course covers image synthesis techniques from perspective of high-end scanline rendering including physically-based rendering algorithms.  Topics:  radiometry, stachastic ray tracing, variance reduction, photon mapping, reflection models, participating media, advanced algorithms for light transport.

title: Introduction to Bioinformatics
subject: Computer Science
description: This course is designed as an introductory course to bioinformatics. The students will be introduced to the concept of bioinformatics and the basic analysis methods used in bioinformatics.

title: Topics in Interdisciplinary Biological and Biomedical Sciences
subject: Computer Science
description: Varying interdisciplinary topics taught by collaborative scientists from UNM, SFI, and LANL.

title: Data Mining Techniques
subject: Computer Science
description: Introductory topics in data mining including: clustering, classification, outlier detection and association-rule discovery. Advanced topics: technologies for data mining, algorithms for mining rich data types and applications of mining algorithms.

title: Complex Adaptive Systems
subject: Computer Science
description: A graduate introduction to computational tools to measure, simulate and analyze complexity in biological and social systems. Topics include cellular automata, dynamical systems, genetic algorithms and other biologically inspired computational methods. Programming maturity is required.

title: Principles of Artificially Intelligent Machines
subject: Computer Science
description: Survey of artificial intelligence exclusive of pattern recognition. Heuristic search techniques, game playing, mechanical theorem proving, additional topics selected by the instructor.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to principles and practice of systems that improve performance through experience. Topics include statistical learning framework, supervised and unsupervised learning. Bayesian analysis, time series analysis, reinforcement learning, performance evaluation and empirical methodology; design tradeoffs.

title: Geometric and Probabilistic Methods in Computer Science
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to applied mathematics for computer scientists. Specific topics include discrete and continuous random variables (including transformation and sampling), information theory, Huffman coding, Markov processes, linear systems theory, Fourier transforms, principal component analysis, and wavelet transforms.

title: Experimental Methods in Computer Science
subject: Computer Science
description: An introduction to experimental methods in Computer Science.

subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to parallel scientific and data intensive programming architectures and systems. Performance issues, speed-up and efficiency. Parallel programming issues and models: control parallel, data parallel and data flow. Programming assignments on massively parallel machines.

description: This class will focus on proactive security i.e. designing networks, algorithms and data structures which are probably robust to attack. Grades will be based on class participation, presentations, and class projects.

subject: Computer Science
description: Current trends in design and philosophy of languages and systems. Data abstraction, data flow languages, alternative control structures, environments, correctness, software tools.

title: Individual Study-Graduate
subject: Computer Science
description: Guided study, under the supervision of a faculty member, of selected topics not covered in regular courses. Restriction: permission of instructor.

subject: Computer Science
description: Syntax analysis and semantic processing for a block-structured language. Lexical analysis, symbol tables, run-time management. Students will write a compiler.

title: Advanced Topics in Compiler Construction
subject: Computer Science
description: Aspects needed to write production quality compilers. Optimization, error recovery, parse table compression, semantic processing of complex data structures, type checking, run-time support, code generation, compiler-writing systems.

title: Advanced Declarative Programming
subject: Computer Science
description: Continued study in one of the declarative programming paradigms: functional, logic, or constraint programming. Specialized techniques are introduced with a view towards general principles.

title: Software Foundations
subject: Computer Science
description: Introduction to modern programming techniques and programming language features and the theory used to describe and define programming languages, using types as the organizational principle.

title: Algorithms-Data Structure
subject: Computer Science
description: Study of data structures and algorithms and mathematics needed to analyze their time and space complexity. Topics include: amortized analysis and self-adjusting data structures for trees and priority queues, graphing algorithms, greedy and divide-and-conquer paradigms.

description: Introduction to database management systems. Emphasis is on the relational data model. Topics covered include query languages, relational design theory, file structures and query optimization. Students will implement a database application using a nonprocedural query language interfaced with a host programming language.

title: Topics in Database Management
subject: Computer Science
description: A continuation of 464/564 with emphasis on query optimization, leading-edge data models, transaction management and distributed databases. Additional topics determined by student interests.

title: Principles and Applications of Big Data
subject: Computer Science
description: This course explores data analysis and management techniques, which applied to massive datasets are the cornerstone that enable real-time decision making in distributed environments, business intelligence, and scientific discovery at large scale.

title: Introductory Numerical Analysis: Numerical Linear Algebra
subject: Computer Science
description: Direct and iterative methods of the solution of linear systems of equations and least squares problems. Error analysis and numerical stability. The eigenvalue problem. Descent methods for function minimization, time permitting.

title: The Specification of Software Systems
subject: Computer Science
description: A comparative study of the techniques used to specify software systems. The course will emphasize formal techniques and will cover the specification of sequential and concurrent systems. Although no programming will be required, students will be required to write specifications for several small software systems.

title: Computer Networks
subject: Computer Science
description: A theoretical and practical study of computer networks, including network structures and architectures; protocols and protocol hierarchies; error handling; routing; reliability; point-to-point networks; broadcast networks; local area networks; efficiency and throughput; communications technologies; case studies.

title: Advanced Operating Systems
subject: Computer Science
description: Theory of design of operating systems. Modeling, simulation, synchronization, concurrency, process hierarchies, networks and distributed systems.

title: Topics in Computer Science for Non-Majors-Graduate
subject: Computer Science
description: This course is intended to provide students in other disciplines with an opportunity to study aspects of modern computer science, tailored to their own field of study. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Special Topics-Graduate
subject: Computer Science
description: Graduate seminars in special topics in computer science. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Colloquium
subject: Computer Science
description: Required of all graduate students. May be repeated, with at most 2 credits towards the M.S. requirements and at most 2 further credits towards the Ph.D. requirements. Students will write a short essay on the topic of one or more of the colloquia offered that semester. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

description: This course will cover advanced topics in Computer Science.

subject: Computer Science
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Computer Science Research Practicum
subject: Computer Science
description:
Develop and practice the skills required to conduct an independent research project. Intended for graduate students pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science.
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Computer Science.

title: Reading and Research
subject: Computer Science

title: Circuit Analysis I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Basic elements and sources. Energy and power. Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's laws. Resistive networks, node and loop analysis. Network theorems. First-order and second-order circuits. Sinusoidal sources and complex representations: impendance, phasors, complex power. Three-phase circuits.  

Pre- or corequisite: PHYS 1320.

title: Instrumentation
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Introduction to laboratory practices and the use of test equipment. Measurements on basic electrical components, dc and ac circuits using ohmmeters, voltmeters, ammeters and oscilloscopes. Circuit simulation.

title: Circuit Analysis II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Analysis of balanced three-phase circuits. Laplace transform with applications to circuit analysis. Passive and active filters. Fourier series and Fourier transform analysis. The two-port circuits.

title: Intermediate Programming and Engineering Problem Solving

title: Computer Logic Design
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering

title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: First and second order Ordinary Differential Equations are solved with various methods including Laplace Transforms, matrices, eigenvalues and other techniques involving linear algebra. Applications will be emphasized using MATLAB.

title: Signals and Systems

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Electronics I

title: Electronics II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Analysis, design, and characterization of linear circuits including operational amplifiers. Design of biasing and reference circuits, multistage amplifiers, and feedback circuits. 

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
An introduction to data structures and algorithms. Topics include asymptotic notation recurrence relations, sorting, hash tables, basic priority queues, balanced search trees and basic graph representation and search. 

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Course considers design principles, implementation issues, and performance evaluation of various software paradigms in an integrated computing environment. Topics include performance measurement and evaluation, program optimization for the underlying architeccture, integration and security for large-scale software systems.

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Intermediate Logic Design
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Probabilistic Methods in Engineering
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Introduction to probability, random variables, random processes, probability distribution/density functions, expectation, correlation, power spectrum, WSS processes, confidence internals, transmission through LTI, applications of probability. 

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Communication Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Amplitude/frequency modulation, pulse position/amplitude modulation, probabilistic noise model, AWGN, Rice representation, figure of merit, phase locked loops, digital modulation, introduction to multiple access systems.

title: Microprocessors

This is a double-starred (**) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program outside of the department. A graduate student enrolled in a double-starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering

Root-locus techniques. Design via gain adjustment. Frequency response techniques. Nyquist criterion, stability margins.

title: Electromagnetic Fields and Waves
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Maxwell’s equations, plane wave propagation, waveguides and transmission lines, transient pulse propagation and elementary dipole antenna.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Introduction to quantum mechanics, crystal structures, insulators, metals, and semiconductor material properties, PN junction, field effect devices.

title: Introduction to Electric Power Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Provides in-depth look at various elements of power systems including power generation, transformer action, transmission line modeling, symmetrical components, pf correction, real/quadrature power calculations, load flow analysis and economic considerations in operating systems.

title: Reinforcement Learning
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Course introduces the theory and practice of reinforcement learning and decision-making techniques, with applications such as communications, computing, control, caching (4C) systems, IoT, cyber physical social systems, quantum communications and computing, smart grid systems, and positioning, navigation, and timing solutions.

title: Senior Design I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Design methodology and development of professional project-oriented skills including communication, team management, economics, and engineering ethics. Working in teams, a proposal for a large design is prepared in response to an industrial or in-house sponsor.

title: Senior Design II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Continuation of 419. Students work in teams to implement 419 proposal. Prototypes are built and tested to sponsor specifications, and reports made to sponsor in addition to a Final Report and Poster Session presentation.

title: Analog Electronics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering

title: VLSI Design
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Advanced topics include: lC technologies, CAD tools, gate arrays, standard cells and full custom designs. Design of memories, PLA, I/0 and random logic circuit. Design for testability.

title: Software Engineering
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Management and technical issues including business conduct and ethics related to the design of large engineering projects. Student teams will address the design, specification, implementation, testing and documentation of a large hardware/software project. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Computer Operating Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Fundamental principles of modern operating systems design, with emphasis on concurrency and resource management. Topics include processes, interprocess communication, semaphores, monitors, message passing, input/output device, deadlocks memory management, files system design. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Design of Computers
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Computer architecture; design and implementation at HDL level; ALU, exception handling and interrupts; addressing; memory; speed issues; pipelining; microprogramming; introduction to distributed and parallel processing; buses; bus protocols and bus masters. CAD project to include written and oral presentations. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Digital Signal Processing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Bilateral Z transforms, region of convergence, review of sampling theorem, aliasing, the discrete Fourier transform and properties, analysis/design of FIR/IIR filters, FFT algorithms spectral analysis using FFT. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Computer Networks
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Theoretical and practical study of computer networks, including network structures and architectures. Principles of digital communications systems. Network topologies, protocols and services. TCP/IP protocol suite. Point-to-point networks; broadcast networks; local area networks; routing, error and flow control techniques. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Wireless Communications
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
The course is an introduction to cellular telephone systems and wireless networks, drawing upon a diversity of electrical engineering areas. Topics include cellular concepts, radio propagation, modulation methods and multiple access techniques. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Quantum Information Science
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An introduction to the mathematical formalism of quantum information science, with an exploration of the key results from its application to quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum metrology.

title: Design of Feedback Control Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Introduction to design of feedback control systems. Design of compensators in the frequency and time domains. PID control and tuning. Digital implementation of analog controllers. Sensitivity and robust performance. Laboratory exercises using Matlab/Simulink and LabVIEW. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Introduction to Microwave Engineering
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This lecture/laboratory course provides essential fundamentals for rf, wireless and microwave engineering. Topics include: wave propagation in cables, waveguides and free space; impedance matching, standing wave ratios, Z- and S- parameters.

title: Advanced Optics I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Electromagnetic theory of geometrical optics, Gaussian ray tracing and matrix methods, finite ray tracing, aberrations, interference and diffraction. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Laser Physics I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Resonator optics. Rate equations; spontaneous and stimulated emission; gas, semiconductor and solid state lasers, pulsed and mode-locked laser techniques. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Antennas for Wireless Communication Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Aspects of antenna theory and design; radiation from dipoles, loops, apertures, microstrip antennas and antenna arrays.

title: Materials and Devices II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An intermediate study of semiconductor materials, energy band structure, p-n junctions, metal-semiconductor junctions, and ideal and non-ideal effects in field effect and bipolar transistors.

title: Microelectronics Processing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Materials science of semiconductors, microelectronics technologies, device/circuit fabrication, parasitics and packaging. Lab project features small group design/fabrication/testing of MOS circuits.

title: Introduction to Electro-Optics and Opto-Electronics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Basic electro-optics and opto-electronics, with engineering applications. Interaction of light with matter. Introduction to optics of dielectrics, metals and crystals. Introductory descriptions of electro-optic, acousto-optic and magneto-optic effects and related devices. Light sources, displays and detectors. Elementary theory and applications of lasers, optical waveguides and fibers. 

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Introduces modern power conversion techniques at a lower level, dealing with basic structures of power converters and techniques of analyzing converter circuits. Students learn to analyze and design suitable circuits and subsystems for practical applications.

title: Photovoltaics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Technical concepts of photovoltaics. Solar cell device level operation, packaging, manufacturing, designing phovoltaic system for stand-alone or grid-tied operation, some business-case analysis and some real-life scenarios of applicability of these solutions.

title: Smart Grid Technologies
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: A detailed study of current and emerging power and energy systems and technologies. Including renewable energies, storage, Smart Grid concepts, security for power infrastructure. Software modeling of power systems and grids.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Professional practice under the guidance of a practicing engineer. Assignments include design or analysis of systems or hardware, or computer programming. A preliminary proposal and periodic reports are required. The engineer evaluates student's work; a faculty monitor assigns grade (12 hours/week) (24 hours/week in summer session). 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering

Restriction: admitted to B.S.Cp.E. Computer Engineering or B.S.E.E. Electrical Engineering.

Restriction: admitted to B.S.Cp.E. Computer Engineering or B.S.E.E. Electrical Engineering.

Restriction: admitted to B.S.Cp.E. Computer Engineering or B.S.E.E. Electrical Engineering.

title: Theory of Linear Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: State space representation of dynamical systems. Analysis and design of linear models in control systems and signal processing. Continuous, discrete and sampled representations. This course is fundamental for students in the system areas.

title: Reinforcement Learning
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Course introduces the theory and practice of reinforcement learning and decision-making techniques, with applications such as communications, computing, control, caching (4C) systems, IoT, cyber physical social systems, quantum communications and computing, smart grid systems, and positioning, navigation, and timing solutions.

title: Optimization Theory
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Introduction to the topic of optimization by the computer. Linear and nonlinear programming. The simplex method, Karmakar method, gradient, conjugate gradient and quasi-Newton methods, Fibonacci/Golden search, Quadratic and Cubic fitting methods, Penalty and Barrier methods.

title: Deep Learning
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Course is an introduction to deep learning, where the theoretical fundamentals of this discipline will be taught. Student will acquire the basic skills necessary to develop their own deep learning designs in Python. Course includes programming in Pytorch and Tensorflow.

title: Nonlinear and Adaptive Control
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Linearization of nonlinear systems. Phase-plane analysis. Lyapunov stability analysis. Hyperstability and Popov stability criterion. Adaptive control systems. Adaptive estimation. Stability of adaptive control systems, backstepping and nonlinear designs.

title: Computer Vision
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Theory and practice of feature extraction, including edge, texture and shape measures. Picture segmentation; relaxation. Data structures for picture description. Matching and searching as models of association and knowledge learning. Formal models of picture languages.

title: Machine Learning
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Decision functions and dichotomization; prototype classification and clustering; statistical classification and Bayes theory; trainable deterministic and statistical classifiers. Feature transformations and selection.

title: VLSI Design
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Advanced topics include: lC technologies, CAD tools, gate arrays, standard cells and full custom designs. Design of memories, PLA, I/0 and random logic circuit. Design for testability.

title: Advanced Machine Learning
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Review of fundamentals of machine learning, classification and regression, unsupervised learning, SLT, support vector machines, kernels, gaussian processes and deep learning. Introduction to Bayes networks, mixture, latent, and Markov models, techniques of variational inference, modern clustering, and latent variable models.

title: Hardware Software Codesign with FPGAs
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
This course provides an introduction to the design of electronic systems that incorporate both hardware and software components. 

Prerequisite: *443.

title: Analog Electronics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Design of advanced analog electronics circuits. BJT and MOSFET operational amplifiers, current mirrors and output stages. Frequency response and compensation. Noise. A/D and D/A converters.

title: Network Economics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course provides an introduction to fundamental concepts in modern networking and networking pricing including the prospect theory, team theory, game theory, contract theory, network externalities and applications in the network economics field.

title: Hardware-Oriented Security and Trust
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course provides an introduction to hardware security and trust primitives and their application to secure and trustworthy hardware systems.

title: Introduction to Technical Cybersecurity
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
This course will cover introductory material around technical cybersecurity in the internet of things. We will cover host-based attacks, network attacks, fuzzing, web attacks, and defenses thereof.
Students in this course should have an undergraduate-level (or equivalent) education in Computer Engineering or Computer Science.

title: Cloud Computing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course provides an introduction to the techniques and technologies used in cloud computing. It consists of independent and intensive hands-on labs. The course emphasizes on architecture and the development of Web services.

title: Introduction to the Internet of Things
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course is an introduction to the Internet of Things (IoT), focusing on integration with cloud technologies, common IoT communication protocols, and embedded Linux.

title: Digital Image Processing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Fundamentals of 2D signals and systems. Introduction to multidimensional signal processing. Applications in digital image processing. Image formation, representation and display. Linear and nonlinear operators in multiple dimensions. Orthogonal transforms representation and display. Image analysis, enhancement, restoration and coding. Students will carry out image processing projects.

title: Plasma Physics I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Plasma parameters, adiabatic invariants, orbit theory, plasma oscillations, hydromagnetic waves, plasma transport, stability, kinetic theory, nonlinear effects, applications.

title: Satellite Communications
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Satellite communication systems provide vital and economical fixed and mobile communication services over large coverage areas. In this course, students learn the fundamentals and techniques for the design and analysis of satellite communication systems.

title: Foundations of Computing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Computational aspects of engineering problems. Topics include machine models and computability, classification and performance analysis of algorithms, advanced data structures, approximation algorithms, introduction to complexity theory and complexity classes.

title: Advanced Computer Architecture
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Course provides an in-depth analysis of computer architecture techniques. Topics include high speed computing techniques, memory systems, pipelining, vector machines, parallel processing, multiprocessor systems, high-level language machines and data flow computers.

title: Digital Signal Processing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Hilbert spaces, orthogonal basis, generalized sampling theorem, multirate systems, filterbanks, quantization, structures for LTI systems, finite word-length effects, linear prediction, min/max phase systems, multiresolution signal analysis.

title: Advanced Networking Topics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Research, design and implementation of high-performance computer networks and distributed systems. High speed networking technologies, multimedia networks, enterprise network security and management, client/server database applications, mobile communications and state-of-the-art internetworking solutions.

title: Probability Theory and Stochastic Processes
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Axiomatic probability theory, projection theorem for Hilbert spaces, conditioned expectations, modes of stochastic convergence, Markov chains, mean-square calculus, Wiener filtering, optimal signal estimation, prediction stationarity, ergodicity, transmission through linear and nonlinear systems, sampling.

title: Digital Communication Theory
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Elements of information theory and source coding, digital modulation techniques, signal space representation, optimal receivers for coherent/non-coherent detection in AWGN channels, error probability bounds, channel capacity, elements of block and convolutional coding, fading, equalization signal design.

title: Introduction to Quantum Information Science
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An introduction to the mathematical formalism of quantum information science, with an exploration of the key results from its application to quantum computing, quantum communication, and quantum metrology.

title: Quantum Error Correction
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course introduces the theory of open quantum systems, quantum noise, and decoherence; discusses the theory of quantum error correction and fault-tolerance to protect quantum computers.

title: Information Theory and Coding
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An introduction to information theory. Fundamental concepts such as entropy, mutual information, and the asymptotic equipartition property are introduced. Additional topics include data compression, communication over noisy channels, algorithmic information theory, and applications.

title: Problems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

title: Introduction to High-Energy-Density Physics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Provides as an introduction, at the graduate level, to the physics of high-energy-density matter, defined by the National Academy of Sciences as matter at pressures greater than 1 Mbar (~ 106 atmospheres).

title: Advanced Optics II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Diffractions theory, coherence theory, coherent objects, and incoherent imaging, and polarization.

title: Foundations of Engineering Electromagnetics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Mathematical foundations for engineering electromagnetics: linear analysis and method of moments, complex analysis and Kramers-Kronig relations, Green's functions, spectral representation method and electromagnetic sources.

title: Pulsed Power and Charged Particle Acceleration
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Principles of pulsed power circuits, components, systems and their relationship to charged particle acceleration and transport. Energy storage, voltage multiplication, pulse shaping, insulation and breakdown and switching. Single particle dynamics and accelerator configurations.

title: Charged Particle Beams and High Power Microwaves
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Overview of physics of particle beams and applications at high-current and high-energy. Topics include review of collective physics, beam emittance, space-charge forces, transport at high power levels, and application to high power microwave generation.

title: Internship in Optical Science and Engineering
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Students do research and/or development work at a participating industry or government laboratory in any area of optical science and engineering.

title: Introduction to Microwave Engineering
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This lecture/laboratory course provides essential fundamentals for rf, wireless and microwave engineering. Topics include: wave propagation in cables, waveguides and free space; impedance matching, standing wave ratios, Z- and S- parameters.

title: Engineering Electrodynamics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic interaction with materials, the wave equation, plane wave propagation, wave reflection and transmission, vector potentials and radiation equations, electromagnetic field theorems, wave propagation in anisotropic media and metamaterials, period structures, dielectric slab waveguides.

title: Electronics RF Design
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course covers radio-frequency (RF) design techniques using transmission lines, strip lines, and solid-state devices. It also includes the design of filters and matching elements required for realizable high-frequency design.  Amplifiers, oscillators, and mixers are covered from an RF perspective.

title: Computational Methods for Electromagnetics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Computational techniques for partial differential and integral equations: finite-difference, finite-element, method of moments. Applications include transmission lines, resonators, waveguides, integrated circuits, solid-state device modeling, electromagnetic scattering and antennas.

title: Guided Wave Optics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Optical propagation in free space, colored dielectrics, metals, semiconductors, crystals, graded index media. Radiation and guided modes in complex structures. Input and output coupling, cross-coupling mode conversion. Directional couplers, modulators, sources and detectors.

title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Detectors
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An intermediate study of semiconductor-based optoelectronic detectors for the ultraviolet-through-THz range of the electromagnetic spectrum.

title: Antennas for Wireless Communications Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Aspects of antenna theory and design; radiation from dipoles, loops, apertures, microstrip antennas and antenna arrays.

title: Optoelectronic Semiconductor Materials and Devices
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Theory and operation of optoelectronic semiconductor devices; semiconductor alloys, epitaxial growth, relevant semiconductor physics (recombination processes, heterojunctions, noise, impact ionization), analysis of the theory and practice of important OE semiconductor devices (LEDs, Lasers, Photodetectors, Solar Cells).

title: Materials and Devices II
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: An intermediate study of semiconductor materials, energy band structure, p-n junctions, metal-semiconductor junctions, and ideal and non-ideal effects in field effect and bipolar transistors.

title: Introduction to Quantum Technology for Chemists and Engineers
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: This course introduces chemistry and engineering students to Quantum Technology, with an emphasis on the role of photonics, chemistry and engineering. Students will gain familiarity with the relevant mathematics, wave electromagnetics, materials systems, and concepts including qubits, coherence, and entanglement.

title: Microelectronics Processing
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Materials science of semiconductors, microelectronics technologies, device/circuit fabrication, parasitics and packaging. Lab project features small group design/fabrication/testing of MOS circuits.

title: Introduction to Electro-Optics and Opto-Electronics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Basic electro-optics and opto-electronics, with engineering applications. Interaction of light with matter. Introduction to optics of dielectrics, metals and crystals. Introductory descriptions of electro-optic, acousto-optic and magneto-optic effects and related devices. Light sources, displays and detectors. Elementary theory and applications of lasers, optical waveguides and fibers.

title: Modern VLSI Devices
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Review of the evolution of VLSI technology and basic device physics. Detailed analysis of MOSFET devices, CMOS device design including device scaling concepts.

title: Fundamentals of Semiconductor LEDs and Lasers
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Carrier generation and recombination, photon generation and loss in laser cavities, density of optical modes and blackbody radiation, radiative and non-radiative processes, optical gain, spontaneous and stimulated emission, Fermi s golden rule, gain and current relations, characterizing real diode lasers, dynamic effects, rate equation; small signal and large signal analysis, radiative intensity noise and linewidth.

title: Power Electronics I
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Introduces modern power conversion techniques at a lower level, dealing with basic structures of power converters and techniques of analyzing converter circuits. Students learn to analyze and design suitable circuits and subsystems for practical applications.

title: Photovoltaics
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Technical concepts of photovoltaics. Solar cell device level operation, packaging, manufacturing, designing phovoltaic system for stand-alone or grid-tied operation, some business-case analysis and some real-life scenarios of applicability of these solutions.

title: Principles and Platforms of Quantum Technology
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
This course provides a deep dive into several implementations of quantum technology, with three goals:
1. Building familiarity with quantum technology platforms and experimental techniques.
2. Understanding the advantages and challenges of quantum systems for communication, sensing, computation.
3. Preparing students to conduct experimental quantum research.

title: Smart Grid Technologies
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: A detailed study of current and emerging power and energy systems and technologies. Including renewable energies, storage, Smart Grid concepts, security for power infrastructure. Software modeling of power systems and grids.

subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description:
Course emphasizes investigation, evaluation, and discussion of areas of specialized knowledge or inquiry relevant to the profession or field of study.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Topics in Interdisciplinary Biological and Biomedical Sciences
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Varying interdisciplinary topics taught by collaborative scientists from UNM, SFI, and LANL.

title: Topics in Algorithms
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Advanced topics including parallel and high-performance computing, multimedia, virtual reality, real-time systems and robotics, encryption and security, information technology, applied algorithmics and computational science algorithms and applications.

title: Topics in Architecture and Systems
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Advanced topics including advanced computer architecture, networks, distributed computing, large-scale resource management, high-performance computing and grid-based computing.

title: Detection and Estimation Theory
subject: Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Hypothesis testing; Karhunen-Loeve representation; optimal detection of discrete- and continuous-time signals; ML, MMSE, and MAP estimation; sufficient statistics, estimation error bounds; Wiener and Kalman-Bucy filtering; detection/receivers for multiuser and multipath fading channels.
