title: Adaptive Tactical Leadership
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Cadets are challenged to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills as they are presented with challenging scenarios related to squad tactical operations.  Cadets receive systematic and specific feeedback on their leadership attibutes and actions.
Corequisite: *301L. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Adaptive Tactical Leadership Lab
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Planning, coordination, execution and evaluation of training and activities with basic course students and ROTC program. Students develop and refine leadership skills in position of responsibility. 
Corequisite: *301. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Leadership in Changing Environments
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Cadets receive increasingly intense situational leadership challenges to build awareness and skilll in leading tactical operations.  Cadets review aspects of combat, stability, and support operations in preparation for the Leadership Development and Assessment. 
Corequisite:  *302L.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Leadership in Changing Environments Lab
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Practice and refinement of leadership skills. Different roles assigned for students at different levels in the program. Planning, coordination, execution and evaluation of training and activities with basic course students and ROTC program. Corequisite: *302.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Military History of the United States
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: The course covers military history from early colonial warfare in the eighteenth century to the global war on terrorism in the twenty-first century. This is a distance learning course. Restriction: instructor permission required.

title: Advanced Directed Studies
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Individual directed studies of advanced subjects under supervision of designated faculty.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Advanced Leadership Seminar
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
Required six week summer internship conducted at Fort Lewis, Washington. Course environment is highly structured and demanding stressing leadership at small-unit level. Course performance weighs heavily in types of commission and branch assignment offered.  
Prerequisite: *301 and *301L and *302 and *302L. Restriction: permission of instructor.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Developing Adaptive Leaders
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:
A course to develop proficiency in planning, executing, and assessing complex operations, functioning as a member of a staff, and providing performance feedback to subordinates.  Cadets assess risk, make ethical decisions, and lead fellow cadets.

title: Leadership in a Complex World
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description:

title: Introduction to Army Leadership I
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course provides an introduction to the Army and basic Soldier skills. Students receive an introduction to the Army Profession and examine what it means to be a professional in the U.S. Army. The overall focus is on developing fundamental knowledge and comprehension of the Army Leadership Requirements Model (ALRM) while understanding the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student. Students also begin learning map reading and land navigation.

title: Introduction to Army Leadership I Lab
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: In this weekly lab, students will apply initial instruction from MLSL 1110 on fieldcraft, first aid, and team building. The lab will be facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IV’s and cadre.

title: Introduction to Army Leadership II
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course introduces students to the personal challenges and competencies that are critical for effective leadership. Students learn how to develop personal life skills such as critical thinking, time management, goal setting, and communication. Students learn the basics of the communication process and the importance for leaders to develop the essential skills to effectively communicate in the Army.

title: Introduction to Army Leadership II Lab
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: In this weekly lab, students will apply initial instruction from MLSL 1110 on fieldcraft, first aid, and team building. The lab will be facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IV’s and cadre.

title: Introduction to Military Fitness I
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course provides a hands-on overview of the fitness requirements needed to serve in the U.S. Army. Students are introduced to, and expected to complete exercises and routines to build their individual strength, endurance, and speed to meet the demands of training and Soldier tasks.

title: Introduction to Military Fitness II
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course provides a hands-on overview of the fitness requirements needed to serve in the U.S. Army. Students are introduced to, and expected to complete exercises and routines to build their individual strength, endurance, and speed to meet the demands of training and Soldier tasks.

title: Foundations of Army Leadership I
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course focuses on leadership and ethics. The course adds depth to the Cadets knowledge of the different leadership styles. Cadets will conduct a leadership analysis of famous leaders and self-assessment of their leadership style. The Army Profession is presented through understanding Culture Awareness, Values, Ethics, and how to apply both to different situations they may encounter as a leader. Army Values and Ethics and their relationship to the Law of Armed Conflict (LOAC) and philosophy of military service are presented through video clips and historical vignettes followed small group discussions with cadets

title: Foundations of Army Leadership I Lab
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: Cadets apply their knowledge outside the classroom in hands-on performance-oriented environments during this weekly lab which is facilitated by MS III Cadets and supervised by MS IVs and cadre.

title: Foundations of Army Leadership II
subject: Military Science & Leadership
description: This course focuses on Army doctrine and decision making. The course begins with analytical techniques, creative thinking skills, and the Army problem-solving process related to situations faced by leaders when making decisions. Troop Leading Procedures (TLPs) and Operations Orders (OPORDs) will lead Cadets to understand Army Doctrine and Symbology.  Squad tactics will be covered in classes on Offensive Operations and Defensive Operations inside of the Army’s operating environmental concept of Multidomain Operations.

title: Foundations of Army Leadership II Lab

title: Foundations of Military Fitness II

description: This course provides a hands-on overview of the fitness requirements needed to serve in the U.S. Army. title: Clinical Practicum: Phlebotomy
subject: Medical Laboratory Technology
description:
Supervised clinical practice in the clinical pathology department of affiliated hospitals. Field laboratory experience in blood sample collection and processing that includes both Venipuncture and capillary puncture techniques. 
Pre- or corequisite: 111 and HCHS 101.

title: Selected Topics in Medical Physics
subject: Medical Physics
description:
The course provides a format to teach current information in medical physics which are not now provided by existing courses. Subject area varies depending upon education in a particular area and the faculty member involved.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Fundamentals of Medical Imaging
subject: Medical Physics
description:
Course provides review of x-ray interactions, x-ray production, film-screen and film processing, mammography, fluoroscopy, image quality, digital radiography, physics of computed tomography, PACS and digital systems, and diagnostic radiation shielding.  
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Medical Imaging Laboratory I X-ray Physics
subject: Medical Physics
description: Perform physics and QA tests on diagnostic x-ray, fluoroscopy, DR systems, CT, mammography, nuclear medicine, MRI, and Ultrasound, and determine how changing setup and variables will affect image quality and patient safety. Evaluate radiation shielding in a diagnostic x-ray rooms.

title: Advanced Medical Imaging
subject: Medical Physics
description:
MR basic physics, MR imaging equipment, and ultrasound imaging physics. Nuclear medicine imaging physics including: radioactive decay, regulations and patient dose calculations.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Medical Imaging Laboratory II MR Ultrasound and Nuclear Imaging Physics
subject: Medical Physics
description:
Perform MRI ACR QC tests and Ultrasound ACR QA tests. Perform QC tests on dose calibrator, gamma camera, PET camera, SPECT camera. Perform a leak test on a sealed radioactive material source. Visit a PET cyclotron.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Radiation Biology for Engineers and Scientists
subject: Medical Physics
description:
Covering fundamentals of the biological effects of ionizing radiation on living systems, especially man; basic biological mechanisms which bring about somatic and genetic effects; and the effect of ionizing radiation on cell structures.  
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Radiation Oncology Physics
subject: Medical Physics
description: Operation of linear accelerators, measurement of absorbed dose and quality of x-ray beams, dose distribution and scatter analysis, and clinical dose calculations for electron and photon beams.  Techniques such as IMRT, total body irradiation, and SRS are discussed. Brachytherapy treatment planning including HDR, LDR and intravascular treatments are covered.

title: Radiation Oncology Physics Laboratory
subject: Medical Physics
description:
Complete a number of clinical treatment plans, participate in the annual calibration of a linear accelerator, acquire basic photon and electron dose data for a computerized treatment planning system, perform several brachytherapy treatment plans including HDR, and LDR plans, and perform an IMRT QA validation.  
Corequisite: 540. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Practicum
subject: Medical Physics
description: Professional practice experience in radiation protection and environmental measurements in non-traditional settings under the guidance of health physicists and radiation protection engineers. Internship arrangement with a local facility employing health physicists or related personnel such as a national laboratory, analytical facility, or hospital.

subject: Music

subject: Music

subject: Music
description: Twentieth-century theoretical techniques applied analytically to all music of the century. Scales, modes, set-theory, twelve-tone theory, minimalist techniques, timbral design and specific compositional methods (Messaien, Cage, Carter, Stockhausen) will be discussed with some rudimentary ear-training.

title: Opera Studio
subject: Music
description: Study of opera through performance, including improvisational technique, movement and character development. Participation in opera scenes and/or larger productions as assigned. Music-reading proficiency required. Admission by audition; preference given to junior and senior vocal majors.

title: Sinfonia
subject: Music
description:
Conducted string chamber orchestra of violins (1st and 2nd), violas, cellos and string basses. Repertory from pre-baroque through present. Open to all university students and community members by audition. Contact instructor for audition requirements.
Maximum of 8 credit hours allowed toward degrees in the College of Fine Arts, in the College of Education and Human Sciences, and in the B.A. Liberal Arts and B.I.S.I. degrees; maximum of 4 credit hours allowed towards degrees in other colleges.

title: Symphony Orchestra
subject: Music
description:
Study and public performance of symphonic literature. Auditions required. 
Maximum of 8 credit hours allowed toward degrees in the College of Fine Arts, in the College of Education and Human Sciences, and in the B.A. Liberal Arts and B.I.S.I. degrees; maximum of 4 credit hours allowed towards degrees in other colleges.

title: Jazz Band
subject: Music
description: Modern jazz ensemble of 20 or more that performs music representing various styles of big band jazz, rock and pop. Auditions required.

title: Jazz Improvisation II
subject: Music
description: Continuation of 237, focusing on chromaticism, chord alterations (with associated chord/scale implications), execution of ii-V7-I patterns in all minor keys and analysis of transcribed solos of jazz masters.

title: Jazz Improvisation III
subject: Music
description: Continuation of 336, introducing modern jazz compositions containing nonfunctional and polytonal harmony, with appropriate chord-scale implications and jazz vocabulary. Analysis of transcribed solos of modern jazz masters is also required.

title: Jazz Arranging
subject: Music
description: Introduction to jazz arranging and scoring techniques for jazz small groups and big bands. Includes voicing for horns, writing for rhythm sections, reharmonization, standards for score and part preparation.

title: Symphonic Band
subject: Music
description:
The UNM Symphonic Band provides a place for the serious player to explore classic and contemporary repertoire for the wind band. This group is open by audition to talented musicians regardless of academic major. 
Maximum of 8 credit hours allowed toward degrees in the College of Fine Arts, in the College of Education and Human Sciences, and in the B.A. Liberal Arts and B.I.S.I. degrees; maximum of 4 credit hours allowed towards degrees in other colleges.

title: Wind Symphony
subject: Music
description:
Study, rehearsal and performance of original works and transcriptions for wind ensemble, symphonic band and chamber winds. Audition required, but open to all students. 
Maximum of 8 credit hours allowed toward degrees in the College of Fine Arts, in the College of Education and Human Sciences, and in the B.A. Liberal Arts and B.I.S.I. degrees; maximum of 4 credit hours allowed towards degrees in other colleges.

subject: Music

subject: Music

title: String Pedagogy Seminar III
subject: Music
description: Exploration of intermediate student skills and techniques, including three-octave scales, arpeggios, shifting, playing in the upper positions and double stops. Pedagogical approaches of Paul Rolland will be explored. Suzuki Books 5 and 6 will be covered. Course fee required.

title: String Pedagogy Lab III
subject: Music
description: Opportunity for the University of New Mexico student to teach more advanced students in the University of New Mexico Music Preparatory School and beginning orchestra classes. May also teach parent preparation classes.

title: The Beatles' Musical Revolution
subject: Music
description: Examines the development of the historical and musical artistry of the Beatles presented within the framework of aesthetic and social/cultural movement 1957-1970 and their individual contributions.

title: Film Music History
subject: Music
description: A survey of film music history, technology and technique from the silent film era to the present. No musical experience necessary.

title: Digital Music Production and Design II
subject: Music
description: Students will learn recording techniques including microphone choice and placement, room acoustics, and diagramming.  They will also work on signal processing, mixing, and mastering their recordings through creative individual and group projects.

title: Music Pedagogy

May be repeated for credit, no limit, as long as subject matter varies, with permission of department chairperson (or dean). Open only to undergraduates enrolled in the music performance program leading to the Bachelor of Music or Bachelor of Music Education; exceptions may be made with permission of the chairperson of the Department of Music.

title: Music Pedagogy
subject: Music

Open only to undergraduates enrolled in the music performance program leading to the Bachelor of Music; exceptions may be made with permission of the chairperson of the Department of Music.

title: Sixteenth-Century Counterpoint
subject: Music

title: Eighteenth-Century Counterpoint
subject: Music

title: Introduction to Max Programming for Musicians

We will center our work around these building blocks but the execution of your work will be largely driven by your own interests and ambitions. Therefore it is critical that you bring your own energy, creativity and ambition to each project.

subject: Music
description: Investigation of country music from an anthropological and ethnomusicological perspective, utilizing recordings and live performances to put scholarship on country music into conversation with social theory and literature on social class, gender, space/place, racial identities.

title: Mexican Music Beyond Borders
subject: Music
description: A contextual exploration of music traditions from Mexico and Mexican communities across the United States. Concentration is placed on indigenous, folk, popular, and art music traditions from historical, socio-cultural, and aesthetic perspectives.

subject: Music

subject: Music

May be repeated for credit with permission of department chairperson (or dean). Open only to undergraduates enrolled in the music performance program leading to the Bachelor of Music; exceptions may be made with permission of the chairperson of the Department of Music.

title: Navajo Expressive Culture
subject: Music
description: Examination of contemporary Diné (Navajo) politics and art (music, Navajo language, photography, dance, radio, filmmaking, comedy, weaving, poetry).  Weekly guest speakers, readings from ethnomusicology, anthropology, critical indigenous studies. Includes overnight field trip to Navajo Nation.

title: String Pedagogy Seminar IV

title: String Pedagogy Lab IV

title: String Pedagogy Recital
subject: Music
description: Students will perform a half-recital in the community and at UNM. In addition, an intermediate/advanced musical score will be analyzed and discussed for pedagogical points.

title: Digital Music Production and Design III
subject: Music
description: Students will create music by learning to customize analogue and digital synthesizers and developing their own samplers.  Collaborative and individual projects will also allow students to explore advanced signal processing techniques.

title: Digital Music Production and Design IV
subject: Music
description: Students will generate numerous musical works while learning, researching, and presenting upon advanced production techniques with an emphasis on studio-style discussion and critique.
