title: Primary Care of Adults I
subject: Nursing
description: The focus of this course is the care of elderly adults in the primary care setting.  Content includes epidemiology, costs of aging, complexities of physical, neurocognitive, social and functional factors, geriatric pharmacology and common concerns.

title: Primary Care of Adults II
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on assessment, diagnosis, and management of increasingly complex acute and chronic adult health care issues.   Application of the scientific basis for practice, best available evidence and collaborative care are key course components.

title: Primary Care of Adults III
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the assessment and management of individuals with complex medical conditions and special populations of adults and elders. Using a problem based approach, students interpret complex cases and devise evidence-based treatment plans.

title: Case Studies in Diagnostic Reasoning
subject: Nursing
description: Focuses on refining interview skills and applying data from the focused history and physical exam to the development of differential diagnoses in primary care. Developing management plans and documentation of patient encounters is also emphasized.

title: Advanced Health Assessment and Diagnostic Reasoning
subject: Nursing
description: Presents theoretical principles of health assessment throughout the life cycle; introduces problem-based, student-centered learning. Includes methodologies of data gathering and data analysis essential to comprehensive health assessment. Labs provide testing and integration of theory.

title: Antepartum-Postpartum for FNP
subject: Nursing
description: This course will provide students with the skills necessary to conduct antepartum/postpartum visits in primary health care settings.

title: Primary Care of Pediatrics I
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on theories and concepts applied by nurse practitioners in the promotion of health in children with emphasis on health education, prevention, culturally and developmentally appropriate care, within the context of family.

title: Pharmacological Principles of Clinical Therapeutics
subject: Nursing
description: This course presents pharmacologic principles which support safe, evidence-based clinical decision making. Content supports pharmacologic management of primary and acute care problems with consideration of age, genetics, health status, pregnancy, and patient context.

title: Antepartum and Postpartum Care
subject: Nursing
description: Primary Care students study, analyze and apply concepts of management process to ante/postpartum periods. Within cultural and rural context, health maintenance preventive care and health policy throughout the life span is covered. Twelve hrs. lab per week.

title: Primary Care of Pediatrics II
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on management of common primary health care problems of children birth through adolescence, and provides a framework for integrating concepts from the clinical sciences and current evidence base into diagnosis and management.

title: Pediatric Chronic Illness-Special Needs
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on assessment, diagnosis, and evidence-based management of children with chronic illness and special needs and their families. Emphasis is on primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention.

title: Women's Health
subject: Nursing
description: Theories and concepts applied in the promotion of the health of adolescent and adult women. Clinical component is specialty-specific.

title: Adolescent Health
subject: Nursing
description: This course builds on basic health and developmental assessment skills and emphasizes health promotion, anticipatory guidance, and prevention of illness for adolescents. Content includes assessment and management of illnesses affecting adolescents and their families.

title: Intrapartum Care
subject: Nursing
description: Management of labor and birth, triage of complications and cultural dimensions foundational to the nurse-midwifery model of intrapartum care are studied.

title: Newborn Care
subject: Nursing
description: Study of the normal neonate within the cultural structure of the family. Common physiological, pathological problems and their management by nurse-midwife emphasized. Clinical component is specialty-specific. For students pursuing an advanced clinical nursing concentration.

title: Evidence-Based Care in Nurse Midwifery
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on skill-building in the assessment of the quality and relevance of clinical research in obstetrics and midwifery. Evaluation of the current science base and identification of biases and weaknesses therein are required to articulate and support options in women's health care. Current research topics are explored from historical and scientific perspectives.

title: Nurse-Midwifery Professional Practice
subject: Nursing
description: This advanced class in nurse-midwifery standards of professional practice analyzes variations based upon populations, geography, practice teams and delivery systems. Historical and ethical frames are used in the analysis of clinical, organization and international issues.

title: The Evidence Base for APRN Primary Care Practice
subject: Nursing
description: The focus of this course is on analysis of clinical research in primary care practice, including identification of biases and limitations, allowing students to articulate best practices and support clinical decision making in primary care.

title: Management of the Acutely Ill Adult-Gerontology Patient
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the acutely ill adult/gerontology patient. Emphasis is placed on acute and episodic health problems common to the adult/gerontology patient.

title: AG-ACNP Practicum I
subject: Nursing
description:
Introductory skills and concepts of acutely ill adult patients. Evaluation and management of common disease processes of adults in the acute care setting will be included.  
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: Managment of the Complex and Chronically Ill Adult-Gerotonology Patient
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the complex and chronically ill adult/gerontology patient. Emphasis is placed on common complex and chronic health problems.

title: AG-ACNP Practicum II
subject: Nursing
description: This clinical course focuses on the diagnosis, management, and continued care of the complex, acute, and critically ill adult/gerontology patient.

title: Health Promotion, Protection, and Disease Prevention for Acute, Critical or Chronically Ill Adults
subject: Nursing
description:
This course focuses on health promotion, protection and disease prevention in the acutely ill, critical or chronically ill adult. Health promotion strategies, risk stratification, and disease prevention and protection concepts are included. 
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: Management of the Critically Ill Adult-Gerontology Patient
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the critical ill adult/gerontology patient. Emphasis is placed on management of critical illnesses.

title: Advanced Diagnostic and Therapeutic Skills
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on skills such as diagnostic and technical interventions used to diagnose, sustain, or stabilize the acutely ill, complex/chronically ill and/or critically ill adult/gerontology patient.

title: ACNP Clinical Topics I:
subject: Nursing
description:
Covers content related to areas of advanced practice that require specialized training and skills. Student chooses from operating room RN first assistant, flight nursing, disaster management, or specialized acute care topics approved by the instructor. 
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: ACNP Clinical Topics II:
subject: Nursing
description: Builds on ACNP Clinical Topics I. The student continues in the chosen topic of operating room RN first assistant, flight nursing, disaster management, or in the specialized acute care topic approved by the instructor.

title: Psychotherapy, Behavior Change, and Health Promotion-Disease Prevention Across the Lifespan
subject: Nursing
description: Theoretical, foundational knowledge of individual, group, and family therapy, health promotion, disease prevention across the lifespan with focus on motivational interviewing, behavior change, use of cognitive, behavioral, dialectical, solution focused, play, and reminiscence therapy.

title: Integrated Behavioral Health Care and Common Psychiatric Presentations
subject: Nursing
description: Overview of behavioral health assessment in common psychiatric disorders and medical conditions with psychiatric presentations in patients across the lifespan with a focus on integrated care settings, interdisciplinary communication, care coordination within a trauma-informed setting.

title: Advanced Assessment, Neurobiology, and Psychopharmacology Across the Lifespan
subject: Nursing
description: Integration of current neurobiological and psychopharmacological theory and research to assessment of symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan.

title: Diagnosis and Management of Adults for the PMHNP
subject: Nursing
description: Evidence-based assessment, diagnosis, health promotion, management, and evaluation of adults with mental illnesses and addictions by the Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. Emphasis on neurobiology, complex psychopharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments, and culturally-sensitive interventions.

title: Diagnosis and Management of Children and Older Adults for the PMHNP
subject: Nursing
description: Psychiatric-mental health assessment, diagnosis, health promotion, management, and evaluation of children, adolescents, and older adults for the PMHNP. Emphasis on complex individual, family, and group therapies, neurobiology, psychopharmacological treatment, and developmentally and culturally-sensitive interventions.

title: Advanced Practicum I
subject: Nursing
description:
The first in a 3 course clinical sequence for PMHNP students. Minimum of 150 hours supervised clinical practice working with a preceptor to evaluate patients, develop management plans, and facilitate individual and group therapies.

Restriction: permission of advisor.

title: Advanced Practicum II
subject: Nursing
description: The second in a 3 course clinical sequence for PMHNP students. Minimum 150 hours supervised clinical practice working with preceptor to develop higher level competencies in evaluation and management of patients across the lifespan.

title: Graduate Problems
subject: Nursing
description: Independent study and research on a topic agreed upon by instructor and student. Restriction: permission of advisor.

title: Clinical Specialty Practicum
subject: Nursing
description: This course provides application of advanced knowledge of health assessment, pathophysiology, and pharmacology to a clinical specialty site while supervised by a clinician. Principles of quality improvement and caring for vulnerable populations will be explored.

title: Topics
subject: Nursing
description:
Specialized courses about a particular topic in nursing. A variety of topic courses are offered according to demand. Different sections indicate different topic content. 
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: Advanced Practice Seminar
subject: Nursing
description: The focus of the course is entry into practice for the advanced practice nurse. Prerequisite: students must have completed the majority of their clinical courses specific to their concentration.

title: Advanced Fieldwork for the Healthcare Educator
subject: Nursing
description:
A minimum of 4 field work credits is required. Taken after core and specialty required courses in the concentration have been completed. Students enroll with faculty in specialty area. Faculty member oversees experience and monitors students progress. 3 lab hours per week, per credit. 
Restriction: permission of advisor.

title: Applied Examination
subject: Nursing
description:
Comprehensive examination taken during the final term of the course of study for completion of Plan II requirements. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: Nursing Thesis I
subject: Nursing
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only. Restriction: permission of advisor.

title: Philosophical Foundations of Nursing Science
subject: Nursing
description:
This course prepares PhD students in nursing and health sciences to analyze and evaluate scientific practice through a variety of philosophical perspectives. Epistemological, logical, cultural, and historical foundations of modern sciences and scientific methods are emphasized.
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or permission of instructor.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Research
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the role of theory in the design and interpretation of research. Emphasis is placed upon mid-range, multidisciplinary theories relevant to research and the application of theory to the student's research.

title: Quantitative Methods in Health Research
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the critical analysis and application of quantitative research designs and methods used to study clinical problems and health policy issues. Emphasis is on survey methods, non-experimental, quasi-experimental and experimental designs.

title: Qualitative Methods in Health Research
subject: Nursing
description:
Exploration of major methodological traditions and techniques of qualitative research and their applications to knowledge development in nursing and health research. 
Restriction: admitted to M.S.N. or Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or NURCP Nursing Certificate.

title: Rural and Cultural Health
subject: Nursing
description:
Rural and cultural health analyzes unique characteristics, current issues, cultural competence and future trends for professional nursing in rural environments. Learning strategies incorporate critical reflection, dialogue, analysis and synthesis of ideas, problem-solving, rural experiences and the creative expression of thought. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Health Outcomes Research
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the advanced analysis and application of quantitative research designs and methods to study patient-centered outcomes and the comparative effectiveness of therapies, health interventions, and systems of healthcare delivery.

title: Mixed Methods Research
subject: Nursing
description: This course provides doctoral students with specific knowledge needed to design and implement a mixed methods research proposal, and assist students to develop critical evaluation skills to critique peer-reviewed mixed methods research reports.

title: Critical Ethnography and CBPR in Health Care Research
subject: Nursing
description: Examines conceptual/philosophical traditions, foundations, characteristics, procedures, applications and contexts [including health disparities/inequities] for health care research involving critical ethnographic and CBPR methods. Focuses on strategies for designing and implementing studies in multicultural settings and diverse populations.

title: Health Care Statistics I
subject: Nursing
description:
Provides the student with knowledge, skills, and practice in performing, analyzing, and interpreting quantitative data. Course content will include descriptive data analysis as well as parametric and nonparametric statistical tests of association and differences. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Health Care Statistics II
subject: Nursing
description: Provides knowledge, skills and practice analyzing and interpreting quantitative data using multivariate statistical techniques, including: multiple linear and logistic regression, factorial analysis of variance and covariance, and exploratory factor analysis.

title: Advanced Qualitative Methods
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on advanced techniques for qualitative research design and data analysis. Emphasis is on the development of a theoretically-­‐informed research approach and essential research skills. The course focuses on the design and conduct of qualitative research, with attention to the historical and community contexts of research and its applications.

title: Health Policy, Politics, and Research
subject: Nursing
description:
This course focuses on health policy, politics, and research. It examines policy stakeholders' use of different types of evidence to influence policy outcomes. Emphasis on U.S. national policies and the affects on health politics and policies.
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice or permission of instructor.

title: Understanding Health Disparities in Policy and Research
subject: Nursing
description: The course focuses on the impact of determinants of health and health disparities in the U.S. It examines quantitative and qualitative research approaches to the study of health disparities and explores policy and research approaches to advance health equity.

title: Health Care Economics
subject: Nursing
description: This course examines concepts, theory, and methods of analysis used in health economics. Emphasis on health policy decision making. Examines the impact of health economic policies on access, cost, quality, and delivery of health care.

title: Health Policy Field Placement
subject: Nursing
description: Building upon objectives from NURS 648, Health Policy, students in the health policy concentration apply knowledge from prior courses in health policy, research methods, and other areas through field placements in public or private sector settings.

title: Disaster Science and Health Equity
subject: Nursing
description: This course assesses the principles of disaster science and health equity in the context of recent disasters and public health emergencies. As an initial course in the program of study, students will learn how the science of nursing, medicine, public health, environmental science, and social science interact during the disaster cycle.

title: Issues in Disaster Health Care
subject: Nursing
description: This course explores issues in disaster health care and policy and links them to specific disasters in the last 100 years. Major disasters will be explored in detail including the impacts on human health especially for at-risk populations, policy at the time of the disaster, and subsequent changes, and notable impacts of health and the healthcare system and nursing. The evolution of both core competencies and crisis standards of care will be explored along with ethical considerations that have arisen. Finally, the course will explore worker health and safety during a disaster and ways to improve both while ensuring the organization’s capacity for disaster.

title: Impacts of Climate Change on Disaster Risk and Health
subject: Nursing
description: This course explores concepts in climate science, and policy and links them to an overview of public health and epidemiology. Specific ways that climate change impacts human health especially for at-risk populations will be covered including heat-related illnesses, health impacts of extreme weather, respiratory and vector-borne diseases, water- and foodborne illnesses, malnutrition, mental health conditions, and the health impacts of population displacement. The intersections between climate change and healthcare and public health with healthcare providers perceptions about how climate change impacts patient health, the responsibility to advocate for climate action, and necessary education and research.

title: Environmental Health Science
subject: Nursing
description: A comprehensive study of the major topics of environmental health, including a background of environmental epidemiology, environmental toxicology, and environmental policy and regulation; Environmental diseases; and applications and domains of environmental health.

title: Disaster Theory and Research Methods
subject: Nursing
description: This course develops competency in principles of research and theory in emergency and disaster management. The course builds on graduate level research and statistic courses.

title: Contemporary Threats of Terrorism and War
subject: Nursing
description: This course familiarizes participants with major contemporary threats from terrorism, violent extremism, and war and develop an understanding and familiarity with the range of capabilities available to nation states to defeat/minimize threats and strategies for responding to a terrorist event.

title: Disaster Health Education and Communication
subject: Nursing
description: The purpose of this course is to familiarize participants with the major concepts of disaster health education and risk communication before, during and after a disaster and to learn how to create appropriate/targeted disaster health education and risk communications.

title: Population Focused Health and Human Services Impact from Disasters
subject: Nursing
description: The purpose of this course is to familiarize participants with issues related to population health and human services impacts from disasters.

title: Refugee Health
subject: Nursing
description: This course familiarizes participants with issues related to refugees and the complex issues (health, legal, social determinants of health, repatriation, local integration, resettlement, etc.) affecting them and the role of nurses and health professions in the provision of care.

title: Complex Humanitarian Disasters
subject: Nursing
description: The purpose of this course is to familiarize participants with issues related to complex humanitarian disasters, the need for interdisciplinary and agency (usually global) coordination and response and minimum protections and standards as describe in the Sphere Handbook.

title: Ph.D. Seminar
subject: Nursing
description:
Specialized courses about a particular topic applicable to advanced graduate students. Different sections indicate different topic content.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Independent Study
subject: Nursing
description:
Intensive, directed study at the doctoral level on a specific topic or issue pertaining to nursing. The focus for this independent study, objectives, and strategies to achieve the objectives are agreed upon by instructor and student. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Topics
subject: Nursing
description:
Specific topics relevant to Ph.D. studies in nursing, as identified by the course title. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing.

title: Research Practicum
subject: Nursing
description:
Focuses on development of skills and techniques for the conduct of research through active participation in faculty research. Emphasis on practical application of research skills and growth in knowledge related to the conduct of research. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing or D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Dissertation
subject: Nursing
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a doctoral dissertation.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only. 
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Nursing.

title: Introduction to Professional Inquiry
subject: Nursing
description: This course will focus on the professional competencies of the DNP for advanced nursing practice emphasizing theory, health equity, professionalism, reflective practice, and professional concepts.

title: Introduction to Translational Evidence-Informed Care
subject: Nursing
description: This course will provide a foundation of patient-centered evidence-informed practice. Students will obtain the essential skills to perform a literature search, appraise the literature, and synthesize evidence to support healthcare related problems, along with understanding various evidence-based practice models.

title: Applied Epidemiology in Advanced Nursing Practice
subject: Nursing
description:
Using group discussion, literature reviews, and primary and secondary data services, students will gain knowledge regarding the historical dimensions leading to health disparities, social injustice, and concepts of marginalization, poverty, race, class, and gender.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Applied Clinical Research in Advanced Nursing Practice
subject: Nursing
description:
This course will focus on the systematic examination and application of health-related research in relation to advanced nursing practice, including clinical practice, nursing and health care administration, community and public health, or health policy.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: The Business and Policy of Practice and Their Influence on the U.S. Health Care System
subject: Nursing
description: The complexities of the U. S. health care system are examined with a focus on the major core changes and challenges affecting health care economics, public health care, policy, health reform, care provisions and workforce issues that affect the health of the population, as well as the cost of care and access to care.

title: Organizational Systems and Quality Management for Advanced Nursing Practice
subject: Nursing
description:
Advanced practice nursing student will focus on the process of quality management, improvement, and outcomes through management and coordination of care in ambulatory and in-patient organizational systems. Individual settings and system-wide performance improvement plans will be developed. 
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Formulating Strategies for Systemic Health Inquiry
subject: Nursing
description: This course will address population health trends and risk factors, population data, social and economic determinants underlying health disparities, community assessment and analysis, as well as statistics used with epidemiological analysis and associated databases.

title: Evidence-Informed Practice and Scholarship
subject: Nursing
description: This course will focus on designing, implementing, delivering, and evaluating community oriented, patient-centered evidence-informed practice methodologies in a variety of settings. Students will learn to use implementation science and translational research to guide solutions to identified healthcare problems.

title: Integrating Innovative Strategies for Systemic Health Change
subject: Nursing
description: This course builds on personal and population health strategies to expand inquiry about innovation, policies, and ethical considerations that influence health. Using innovation, information and communication technologies, and informatics processes; construct strategies to manage and improve health outcomes across systems.

title: Translation of Evidence for Healthcare Practice, Policy, and Evaluation
subject: Nursing
description: The course will build on previous knowledge in literature review, research assessment and appraisal, quality improvement and analytic methodology, statistical analysis, policy design and implementation, systems theory, and evidence-based practice frameworks.

title: Advanced Pathophysiology
subject: Nursing
description: The course focuses on the application of analytical reasoning and problem solving based on pathophysiology and clinical presentations of a broad variety of diseases of children and adults across the lifespan for advanced nursing practitioner.

title: Pharmacological Principles of Clinical Therapeutics
subject: Nursing
description: The focus of this course is on principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics which support safe, evidence-based clinical decision making. Knowledge of clinical therapeutics, including drug categories essential for pharmacologic management of primary and acute care problems, is also emphasized. Content includes pharmacologic considerations related to age, genetics, health status, pregnancy / lactation, and patient context.

title: Advanced Health Assessment
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on theories and concepts applied by nurse practitioners in assessment across the lifespan.

title: Primary Care Concepts
subject: Nursing
description: This course explores concepts such as: principles of justice – diversity, equity and inclusion,  integration of anti-racism, determinants of health into strategies for building therapeutic relationships, and interdisciplinary collaboration in health supervision/  promotion, and disease prevention.

title: Genetics and Genomics for Advanced Practice Nursing
subject: Nursing
description: This course provides an overview of the role of genetics and genomics in health and illness for integration and application in advanced practice nursing.

title: Diagnostic Reasoning
subject: Nursing
description: This course supplements content from the advanced health assessment course. Students utilize data obtained in the history and physical exam for development of differential diagnoses, management plans and documentation common to primary care.

title: Mental Health in Primary Care
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on integration of current neurobiological, pathophysiological, and psychopharmacological evidence for symptom assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of common mental health disorders across the lifespan and in diverse populations.

title: Etiology and Management of Complex Health and Illness in Rural Health
subject: Nursing
description: This course examines complex health and illness in individuals in a rural health setting with an emphasis on multi-system processes, environmental, nutritional, economic, cultural, psychosocial stressors, and genetic influences.

title: Professional Concepts and Issues for Advanced Nursing Practice
subject: Nursing
description:
This course presents the student with the opportunity to explore professional concepts and issues in advanced professional nursing practice and health care and incorporate them into their practice.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Principles of Advanced Nursing Management
subject: Nursing
description:
This course introduces the importance of management skills, identifies essential management skills, and presents a learning model for developing management skills. Essential management skills are organized into three categories: personal, interpersonal, and group.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Leading Organizational Change
subject: Nursing
description:
Integrated learning experiences explore leadership challenges in changing workplaces through on-site implementation of capstone projects. Executive leadership is discussed in context of the role of the nurse leader in promoting and managing institutional change.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Health Care Innovations and Informatics
subject: Nursing
description:
This course focuses on nursing informatics. Topics include: (1) introduction to the nursing informatics; (2) health care informatics applications; (3) evidence-based decision support; (4) information systems design; and (5) new opportunities and emerging trends.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Primary Care of Adults I
subject: Nursing
description: This is the first in a three-course sequence focusing on primary care competencies in the adult/geriatric population. Students learn patient-centered assessment, diagnostic reasoning, and beginning management of common conditions presenting to primary care settings.

title: Primary Care of Adults II
subject: Nursing
description: This is the second in a three-course sequence focusing on primary care competencies in the adult/geriatric population. This course builds skills in assessment, diagnosis, and management of increasingly complex acute and chronic health care issues.

title: Primary Care of Adults III
subject: Nursing
description: This is the third in a three-course sequence focusing on primary care competencies in the adult/geriatric population. Using a problem-based approach, students further skills in evidence-informed management of complex medical conditions and special populations.

title: Sexual and Reproductive Health Across the Lifespan
subject: Nursing
description: Prepare students in the foundation of client-centered assessment, diagnostic reasoning, and management of common conditions seen in adolescents and adults presenting to primary care settings for sexual, perinatal, and reproductive health concerns.

title: Clinical Skills and Procedures in Primary Care
subject: Nursing
description: This course provides students with development of technical skills needed when providing procedures commonly offered in primary and urgent care settings for patients across the lifespan.

title: Introduction to Pediatric Physical and Developmental Assessment
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on theories and concepts applied by nurse practitioners in the area of pediatric assessment.

title: Advanced Pediatric Physical and Developmental Assessment
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the application of advanced pediatric assessment theories and concepts by nurse practitioners.

title: Case Studies in Pediatric Diagnostic Reasoning
subject: Nursing
description: Course provides students with focused pediatric diagnostic reasoning skills including application of knowledge during simulated patient encounters.

title: Primary Care of Pediatrics I
subject: Nursing
description: Course focuses on health promotion across the pediatric lifespan including education, prevention, and culturally and developmentally appropriate care in the context of the family.

title: Primary Care of Pediatrics II
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the evaluation and management of common health care problems across the pediatric lifespan with an emphasis on differential diagnosis and collaboration in primary care.

title: Adolescent and Behavioral Health
subject: Nursing
description: Course covers primary care for adolescents including health promotion, illness prevention for common health problems including behavioral health problems.

title: Pediatric Special Populations
subject: Nursing
description: Course focuses on evidence-informed management of complex acquired or inherited pediatric conditions and adolescent primary care.

title: Specialty Pediatric Clinical Practicum
subject: Nursing
description: Course builds upon the student’s proficiency in comprehensive health evaluation and management in pediatric healthcare.

title: Fundamentals of Reproductive Health and Primary Care Across the Lifespan
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the physical, mental, genetic, environmental, sexual, and social wellbeing of women from adolescence through the lifespan.  The student will develop fundamental skills of reproductive health and whole person wellness using national recommendations and evidence-based practices.

title: Midwifery in Action; Historical and Scientific Perspectives
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on grounding nurse-midwifery students in the history of midwifery in the United States and in international maternal-child health, as well as the evidence-base for midwifery care in diverse settings.

title: Complex Reproductive Healthcare
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the complex reproductive and sexual health of women from adolescence through the lifespan.  Public health recommendations and evidence-based practices will be utilized to formulate safe and effective treatment plans in partnership with clients.

title: Midwifery Care for Pregnancy and Postpartum
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on theories and concepts applied by nurse-midwives in the promotion of health for childbearing people in the antepartum and postpartum periods of the reproductive cycle including cultural and rural context, health maintenance, preventive care, and policy considerations.

title: Foundations of Childbirth
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on concepts and evidence which frame techniques and skills required for safe labor and birth and management of the immediate postpartum period including skill development in techniques for labor, birth, third, fourth stage and the postpartum period.

title: Midwifery Care for Childbirth
subject: Nursing
description: This course will focus on clinical midwifery care of laboring persons and the fetus including facilitation of labor and birth and the management of birth and postpartum care, as well as acute emergencies and obstetrical triage.

title: Fundamentals of Newborn Care
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the delivery of well childcare and the management of common primary health care problems of the normal infant from birth through one month of age. The antepartum and intrapartum prediction of neonatal health problems by the nurse midwife are also emphasized.

title: Midwifery Care of the Newborn
subject: Nursing
description: This clinical course focuses on the delivery of well childcare and the management of common primary health care problems of the normal infant from birth through one month of age including antepartum and intrapartum prediction of neonatal health problems.

title: Advanced Diagnostic Test Interpretation
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on interpretation of advanced diagnostic tests necessary for the advanced practice nurse to diagnose health issues and direct care management. Topics will include 12 Lead EKGs, radiographic imaging, ultrasound, and CT scans.

title: Managing the Acute & Complex/Chronically Ill Adult/Gerontology Patient I
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the complex/chronically ill adult gerontology patient presenting with acute illness.  Emphasis will be placed on the cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurological, psychiatric, and renal, endocrine systems.

title: Managing the Acute and Complex/Chronically Ill Adult/Gerontology Patient II
subject: Nursing
description: This course is part 2 of 2 courses focusing on the complex/chronically ill adult gerontology patient presenting with acute illness.  Emphasis will be placed on the gastrointestinal, hematological, integumentary and musculoskeletal systems.

title: Managing Emergency & Critical Illness in the Adult/Gerontology Patient
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on the adult gerontology patient presenting with emergency and/or critical illness.  Emphasis will be placed on advanced cardiovascular hemodynamics, ventilatory management, multisystem trauma, shock states, and critical care issues.

title: AGACNP Practicum I
subject: Nursing
description: This clinical course focuses on the care of the acutely ill adult/gerontology patient.  The AG-ACNP student will have experiences in the acute care setting and develop evidence-informed, person-centered plans of care.

title: AGACNP Practicum II
subject: Nursing
description: This clinical course focuses on the care of the acutely ill adult/gerontology patient.  The AG-ACNP student will have experiences in various acute care settings & subspecialties and develop plans of care using a collaborative approach.

title: Principles in Advanced Nursing Leadership
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on leadership characteristics and skills required to initiate and sustain a culture of organizational excellence. A broad range of established leadership theories, frameworks, strategies, and ethics in leadership practice are explored.

title: Organizational Excellence Seminar
subject: Nursing
description: Topics by current administrative and/or organizational leaders addressing key management strategies and metrics of organizational excellence for patient experience, provider engagement and satisfaction, staff engagement and satisfaction, finance measures, and community accountability.

title: Transforming Organizations through Healthcare Reform
subject: Nursing
description: This course delves into various inter-relationships, effects, strategies, and methods of healthcare change leader practice through the lens of organizations as complex adaptive systems.

title: Finance for Emerging Nurse Leaders
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on managing financial resources within a continually evolving healthcare environment. A working knowledge of finance concepts and processes provide a framework for basic competency in a healthcare setting.

title: Nursing Admininstrative Leadership Specialty Practicum
subject: Nursing
description: A precepted practice experience incorporating foundational leadership knowledge for the novice to mid-career nurse administrative and/or organizational leader.

title: Human Resources Management
subject: Nursing
description: A journey into human resource management for the nurse leader from addressing the nursing shortage, ethical practice, recruitment, legal implications, retention, onboarding, leader and staff professional development, through succession planning.

title: Finance for Advanced Nurse Leaders
subject: Nursing
description: For the advanced nurse leader, this course provides depth of knowledge in organizational performance improvement, cost effective, cost benefit, and ethical healthcare financing, and financial drivers in healthcare systems.

title: Quality Management for Nurse Leaders
subject: Nursing
description: This course provides an evidence-based systems approach to quality management in healthcare from theoretical, philosophical, and practice-based perspectives.

title: Public Community-Based Program Management and Evaluation
subject: Nursing
description: Students will explore evidence-based evaluation frameworks commonly used by government and philanthropic entities for grant proposal development and program evaluation.

title: Foundations in PMHNP Clinical Assessment and Practice
subject: Nursing
description: Course presents an overview of behavioral health assessment in common psychiatric disorders. The focus is on Trauma-Informed Care, provider wellbeing, reflective practice, crisis intervention, establishing therapeutic relationships, and care coordination across healthcare systems.

title: Psychiatric Diagnostic Reasoning
subject: Nursing
description: Course provides students with a biopsychosocial framework for PMHNPs. Knowledge of diagnosis of psychiatric disorders is emphasized. Students apply knowledge and skills in the differential diagnosis of major psychiatric disorders based on selected taxonomies.

title: Psychotherapy and Behavior Change
subject: Nursing
description: Course presents theoretical and foundational knowledge related to individual, group, and family therapy for PMHNPs. The focus is on forming a therapeutic relationship and applying motivational interviewing and cognitive behavioral therapy techniques.

title: Neurobiology and Psychopharmacology in Psychiatric Disorders
subject: Nursing
description: Course focuses on the integration of current neurobiological, pathophysiological, and psychopharmacological theory and research to the assessment of symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan with psychotropic medication.

title: Advanced Practice Seminar on Leadership Development for the PMHNP
subject: Nursing
description: Course explores the role of the PMHNP as an independently licensed clinician, leader, and member of a comprehensive health care system. Emphasis is on consumer-focused mental health care that is equitable and ethically-driven.

title: Complex Management of Adults for the PMHNP
subject: Nursing
description: Course focuses on evidence-informed psychiatric mental health assessment, diagnosis, and symptom management of adults. There is an emphasis on complex psychopharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments as well as healthcare policy and equitable access to care.

title: Complex Management of Special Populations for the PMHNP
subject: Nursing
description: Course focuses on evidence-informed psychiatric mental health assessment, diagnosis, and symptom management of special populations. There is an emphasis on developmentally and culturally-sensitive psychopharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments interventions for these diverse populations.

title: Advanced Practicum I
subject: Nursing
description: First in a three-course clinical sequence for PMHNP students. Students complete a minimum of 150 hours supervised clinical psychiatric practice evaluating patients and developing management plans. Students will reflect on practice in small group seminars.

title: Advanced Practicum II
subject: Nursing
description: Second in a three-course clinical sequence for PMHNP students. Students complete a minimum of 300 hours supervised clinical psychiatric practice evaluating patients and implementing management plans. Students will reflect on practice in small group seminars.

title: Independent Study
subject: Nursing

Specific intensive directed study at the doctoral level relevant to D.N.P. studies in Nursing.
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: Topics
subject: Nursing

Specific topics relevant to D.N.P. studies in Nursing, as identified by the course title. 
Restriction: admitted to D.N.P. Nursing Practice.

title: DNP Practicum
subject: Nursing

title: Advanced Nursing Fieldwork
subject: Nursing
description: This is the final practicum for the program, focusing on achieving terminal program competencies in the advanced practice role. didactic components of this course facilitate the development of students into independent, docotorally- prepared clinicians and leaders who integrate program content into practice across systems of care.

title: Systems Thinking for Healthcare Transformation I
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on design of the scholarly project. Application and integration of knowledge gained through foundational coursework continues with the implementation of a scholarly project in an identified area of practice to optimize healthcare system outcomes.

title: Systems Thinking for Healthcare Transformation II
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on implementation of the scholarly project. Application and integration of knowledge gained through foundational coursework continues with the implementation of a scholarly project to optimize healthcare system outcomes or care delivery for populations and communities.

title: Systems Thinking for Healthcare Transformation III
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on evaluation of the scholarly project. Application and integration of knowledge gained through foundational coursework continues with the implementation of a scholarly project to optimize healthcare system outcomes or care delivery for populations and communities.

title: Systems Thinking for Healthcare Transformation IV
subject: Nursing
description: This course focuses on dissemination of the scholarly project. Application and integration of knowledge gained through foundational coursework continues with the dissemination of a scholarly project to optimize healthcare system outcomes or care delivery for populations and communities.

subject: Nutrition
description: Overview of nutrition research including study design, basic statistical analyses, interpretation of peer-reviewed research, assessment of study quality, scientific writing for health-professionals focusing on nutrition and dietetics. Application of clinical, epidemiological, translational nutrition research, writing.

title: Clinical Nutrition Assessment and Skills
subject: Nutrition
description:
This course will introduce concepts of nutritional assessment and the practical application of these concepts in the total health care of individuals and gourds in clinical, community, and research settings.

Restriction: admitted to B.S. Nutrition and Dietetics or Post-Baccalaureate program.

subject: Nutrition
description:
Overview of management and leadership principles related to business/entrepreneurial, clinical, community and foodservice nutrition and dietetics professionals with application of marketing, budgeting, human resource issues, staffing and research.
Prerequisite: 2110.

title: Principles of Food Science
subject: Nutrition
description:
Chemical and physical properties of foods, scientific principles of food preparation, objective and sensory evaluation of food modifications. Students design and conduct an independent research project based on food science principles. 
Prerequisite: 2110 and CHEM **301. 
Pre- or corequisite: BIOL 2305. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Nutrition and Dietetics.

title: Energy Nutrients in Human Nutrition
subject: Nutrition
description:
Carbohydrate, fat and protein in human nutrition. Emphasis includes digestion, absorption, metabolism, food sources and dietary recommendations. Implications for health promotion and disease prevention.  
Prerequisite: 2110 and (CHEM 2120 or CHEM **301).

title: Vitamins and Minerals in Human Nutrition
subject: Nutrition
description:
Water and fat-soluble vitamins, macrominerals and trace minerals in human nutrition. Emphasis includes absorption, metabolism, food sources, dietary recommendations, deficiencies and nutrient interactions. Implications for health promotion and disease prevention are explored. 
Prerequisite: 2110 and (CHEM 2120 or CHEM **301).

subject: Nutrition

title: Introduction to Public Health Nutrition
subject: Nutrition
description: Application of community health principles to nutrition programs for individuals and groups. Experiences will include work with community nutrition programs.

title: Nutrition in the Life Cycle
subject: Nutrition
description:
Nutritional assessment, physical growth and development, and the physiological basis for nutrient needs in pregnancy, lactation, infancy, childhood, adolescence and old age. Application to food selection patterns and the influence of social and cultural factors.  
Prerequisite: 2110 and BIOL 2210. 
Restriction: junior standing or higher.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
subject: Nutrition
description: The application of diets in the treatment of impaired digestive and metabolic conditions using the case study approach.

title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
subject: Nutrition
description:
Continuation of Medical Nutrition Therapy I.  
Prerequisite: 427. Restriction: admitted to B.S. Nutrition and Dietetics.

title: Applied Nutrition and Exercise
subject: Nutrition

Advanced studies and research under the supervision of a faculty mentor.

Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of an undergraduate Senior-level thesis.

title: Methods in Nutrition Research
subject: Nutrition
description: Examination of research methodologies; relevant evidence based research and use of appropriate databases. Selection and construction of appropriate data collection techniques, consideration of ethical issues, preparation of a literature review and research proposal.

title: Advanced Medical Nutrition Therapy
subject: Nutrition
description: Application of nutritional sciences, energetics, physiology, biochemistry and metabolism to current topics in clinical nutrition. Evaluation of nutritional assessment of critically ill patients and modifications of diets to meet individual needs.

title: Pediatric Nutrition
subject: Nutrition
description: This course focuses on the unique nutrient needs essential to provide optimal nutritional care for the pediatric population and to advocate for policy change for improved pediatric health outcomes.

title: Prevention and Lifestyle Treatment of Chronic Diseases
subject: Nutrition
description: This is a graduate course with emphasis on a review of current peer-reviewed literature to topics related to prevention and lifestyle treatment of some chronic diseases. The course will explore topics relevant to the improvement of health in individuals and populations.

title: Applied Dietetics Practice
subject: Nutrition

Planned and supervised dietetic experiences in agency or institutional setting. Experiences are based on the Performance Requirements of the Standards of Education developed by the American Dietetic Association.

title: Dietetics Practicum
subject: Nutrition
description:
Students will complete specific Dietetic Intern competencies and activities, attend profession organization events and didactic classes facilitating development of dietetic, professional communication, mentoring, and critical thinking skills. Preparing students for a role on the healthcare team.
Restriction: active status as a Dietetic Intern.

Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.

subject: Nutrition
description: This course provides an overview of general concepts of nutrition, which can be applied to food choices that support a healthy lifestyle. The cultural, psychological, physiological and economic implications of food choices are explored.

title: Human Nutrition
subject: Nutrition
description:
This course provides an overview of nutrients, including requirements, digestion, absorption, transport, function in the body and food sources. Dietary guidelines intended to promote long-term health are stressed.
Prerequisite: BIOL 1140 or BIOL 2110C or CHEM 1120C or (CHEM 1215 and CHEM 1215L).

title: Sea Power
subject: Naval Science
description: This course surveys U.S. naval history from the American Revolution to the present. Included is an in-depth discussion of the geopolitical theory of Mahan and other historical figures. Emphasis is on major developments in naval strategy, tactics, technology and the effects of the relevant political climate.

title: Navy and Marine Corps Fitness
subject: Naval Science
description:
This course will develop, enhance and solidify physical fitness levels of future Navy and Marine Corps officers. It will incorporate various core, cardio and muscle strengthening events.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Navigation
subject: Naval Science
description: Theory, principles and procedure of ship coastal and open-ocean navigation. Included are studies in mathematical analysis, spherical triangulation, publication report logs, and chart preparation. Navigational aids, including inertial systems, radio beacons and satellites are also studied.

title: Naval Operations
subject: Naval Science
description: Naval ship operations, tactical formations and dispositions, relative motion, tactical plots and maneuvering boards are analyzed. Rules of the road, lights and signals are studied.

title: Naval Professional Laboratory
subject: Naval Science
description:
To provide Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps students with the tools and opportunities to ensure service readiness and mission accomplishment; enhance professional and personal growth and development, and enable life-long learning.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Evolution of Warfare
subject: Naval Science
description: Evolution of the basic principles and techniques of warfare throughout history. Relationship of tactics and strategy and the impact of technological developments in selected topics. Emphasis is placed on an understanding of the theoretical principles underlying modern tactics and strategy.

title: Leadership and Management
subject: Naval Science
description: Structure and principles of naval leadership and management. Topics include interrelationship of authority, responsibility, and accountability, prioritization, resource management and group dynamics.

title: Navy and Marine Corps Fitness

This course will develop, enhance and solidify physical fitness levels of future Navy and Marine Corps officers. It will incorporate various core, cardio and muscle strengthening events.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Leadership and Ethics
subject: Naval Science
description: Structure and principles of naval leadership and management in which underlying concepts are examined within the context of American military, social and industrial organization and practice. Emphasis is given to management, leadership, ethics, and human goals functions.

Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Fundamentals of Maneuver Warfare
subject: Naval Science
description: This course prepares future leaders by studying tactical principles, current military developments, and other aspects of warfare. There is a specific focus in United States Marine Corps doctrine and historical case studies.

title: Principles and Concepts of Naval Science
subject: Naval Science
description: Introduction to the naval service, customs, traditions, courtesies and naval officers communities.

title: Naval Professional Laboratory Basic
subject: Naval Science
description: To provide Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps students with the tools and opportunities to ensure service readiness and mission accomplishment; enhance professional and personal growth and development; and enable life-long learning.

title: Navy and Marine Corps Fitness
subject: Naval Science
description: This course will develop, enhance and solidify physical fitness levels of future Navy and Marine Corps officers. It will incorporate various core, cardio and muscle strengthening events derived from Naval and Marine Corps standards.

title: Naval Ship Systems I
subject: Naval Science
description: Introduction to naval engineering systems concepts and practices. Topics include ship design, compartmentation, ship stability, damage control, fire-fighting and ship propulsion systems.

title: Naval Ship Systems II
subject: Naval Science
description: Principles of naval weapons systems. Topics include sensors and detection systems, computational systems, tracking systems, weapon delivery systems, the fire control problem and new developments in weapon systems integration.

title: Introduction to Occupation and Health
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Introduction to understanding occupation and health as it relates to self, clients, and the occupational therapy assessment and intervention process. The emphasis is on richness of occupation including: motivation, meaning, roles, cultural factors and sociental influences.

title: Neuroanatomy
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Anatomy of the brain and spinal cord with emphasis on integration of sensory and motor systems. Synthesis of neuroanatomical, neurochemical and neurophysiological basic science principles relevant to clinical practice in adult and pediatric neurorehabilitation.

title: Kinesiology of Occupation
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Apply the principles of kinesiology and biomechanics to the study of occupations. Arthrology, tissue mechanics, goniometrics, muscle strength testing, kinesiological and biomechanics analysis of occupations will be presented in lecture, lab and problem-based learning formats.

title: Introduction to Evidence-Based Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Introduction to applied research for physical and occupational therapists. The central focus of this course is how information from physical and social science-based research is gathered, analyzed, reported and use to inform evidence-based practice.

title: Occupation Across the LifeSpan
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Review of roles, occupational tasks, models of occupation and developmental theories from infancy to old age. Determinants of occupational performance including cultural influences; physical and social environment; physiological, senory, neuromotor, cognitive and psychological dimensions are reviewed.

title: Relationship Centered Care
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Introduction to the importance of person-centered care in occupational therapy assessment and intervention services to develop an appreciation of the therapeutic relationship and skills to interact with clients holistically, recognizing cultural and psychosocial influences.

title: Applied Occupations: Orthopedic Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Application of occupational therapy concepts and principles to adult populations with physical and orthopaedic conditions is covered along with theoretical foundations underlining person-centered occupations, job analysis and to increase participation in occupations.

title: Graduate Seminar
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
A four-semester seminar sequence that provides structure and support for graduate occupational therapy students to develop professionalism and research experience.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Applied Occupations: Neurological Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Application of occupational therapy concepts to adult populations with physical and neurological conditions is covered, along with theoretical foundations underlining person-centered occupations, job analysis, and the OT process to increase participation in occupations.

title: Applied Occupations: Psychosocial Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: This course covers psychosocial and behavioral dimensions of occupational therapy practice across the lifespan. This course gives students the opportunity to learn about psychological Occupational Theraphy assessments and interventions related to performance.

title: Complex Reasoning in Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
This course addresses the complex process of reasoning in practice to solve occupational problems as they influence health and well-being.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

title: Advocacy, Communication and Leadership
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Advocacy skills (grant writing, marketing and policy formation), communication skills and leadership skills (professional development, professional presentations and leadership roles) as they relate to occupational therapy are emphasized.

title: Scholarship of Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
In this course students will use and evaluate the professional literature surrounding outcome measures and the evidence supporting occupational therapy practice and education.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

title: Neuroscience of Occupation
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: This course emphasizes the application of systems-level, behavioral-level and cognitive-level neuroscience to understanding: a) occupational development across the lifespan and b) the practice of occupational therapy for persons with activity limitations caused by neuropathological conditions.

title: Advanced Leadership and Advocacy
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
Course addresses competencies needed to become a change agent in occupational therapy such as leadership skills and experience, advocacy at multiple levels including public policy and high-level decision making and communication abilities.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

title: Education in Occupational Therapy
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
This course introduces students to concepts of learning theory, applications to practice, assessments, education ethics, curriculum development, and academic leadership within occupational therapy.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

title: Organization and Administration
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: This course will enable students to practice effectively in increasingly complex health care delivery system. Emphasis is on understanding of organizational systems, including program planning, management and reimbursement, as well as legislation and ethics.

title: Teaching Practicum
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: This course provides students with the opportunity to work closely with a faculty member or members to acquire teaching experiences either online, hybrid, and/or face to face in person.

title: Applied Data Management and Research for Clinical Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
This course addresses critical concepts and practical methods to support planning, collections, storage, and dissemination of data to support marketing, evaluate service delivery and clinical research in occupational therapy.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

title: Applied Occupations: Pediatric Practice
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Application of the occupational therapy process to functional problems which interrupt or delay normal growth, development and maturation during infancy, childhood and adolescence. Occupational intervention strategies for children and their families are covered.

title: Community Health
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: The purpose of this course is for the student to gain an increased knowledge of: community-based health considerations and issues; community health resources; partnerships with community services; interdisciplinary processes; and serving people in community settings.

title: Fieldwork II
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Experiences with clients, occupational therapists and professionals in the community. Students must participate in two 12-week, full-time clinical internships. Fieldwork is carried out in various settings in New Mexico and surrounding states. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Independent Study
subject: Occupational Therapy
description: Self-directed learning in occupational therapy with opportunity to explore an area of interest in depth. Develop experience in occupational therapy under the supervision of a faculty mentor and community practitioners.

title: Professional Capstone Project
subject: Occupational Therapy
description:
The professional capstone project offers students the opportunity to use and apply their knowledge of occupational therapy to transform practice. Students will identify the opportunities, limitations, requirements and need of a particular practice environment.

Restriction: admitted to Doctor of Occupational Therapy Program or permission of the Program Director.

Corequisite: 408.

This course focuses on the technical software skills of the online eLearning site administrator as students get practical, hands-on experience using MoodleCloud (MC) and other LMS's.

description: This course is designed to develop your ability to apply research-backed creativity strategies and design thinking in your work, learning, and life; in other words, "in the wild" by documenting your own creative practice.

subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is designed to develop your ability to frame and reframe ill-structured, complex problems, AKA "wicked problems", from your work, learning, and life using research-backed creativity strategies and design thinking methods.

subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences

subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
