subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is designed to develop students understanding in instructional design. Topics will include design thinking, agile design, needs assessment, learner analysis, prototyping, instructional design strategies, formative and summative evaluation methods, and flexibly adaptive approaches.

title: Program Evaluation
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Provides the student with a basic understanding of the evaluation process, the application of evaluations in determining the effectiveness and/or value of a learning experience both in the classroom and in the workplace.

title: Framing Designs for Learning
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is designed to develop students understanding and experience in framing learning design problems. Topics will include design thinking, agile design, needs assessment and problem definition skills including task/content, context, and learner analysis.

title: Prototyping Designs for Learning
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description:
This course is designed to develop student's understanding and experience in systematically designing solutions to learning design problems. Topics will include iteration, prototyping, instructional design strategies, formative and summative evaluation methods, and flexibly adaptive approaches.
Corequisite: 546.

title: Training and Development
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course introduces training techniques suitable for instructing adult learners in a variety of settings. Students learn to create a training environment conducive to learning, design an instructional unit, and develop a training program.

title: Team Development and Facilitation
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Provides learners with information and skill development of various methods and techniques for leading teams in virtual and face-to-face settings. Emphasis is placed on team development and facilitation skills necessary to enhance team performance.

title: The Role of Wisdom in Adult Learning Across Cultures
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course explores the concept of wisdom from various traditions and academic disciplines through weekly lectures, discussions, and experiential activities. It examines the role of wisdom in development and suggests perspectives for fostering wisdom.

title: Consulting and Project Management
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is an introduction to major approaches, concepts, skills, and techniques used in the consulting industry.

title: Mentoring and Adult Career Development
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Students examine adult career patterns and organizational perspectives on employee career development. Specific emphasis is on mentoring and coaching adults in career decision making.

title: Mentoring Network
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Participants will identify their career goals, aspirations, and learning needs. Proximal development activities and gap analysis will guide them in developing a roadmap with strategies to build effective Mentoring Networks and gain the support needed to propel their careers.

title: Human Performance Improvement
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course serves as an introduction to human performance improvement that applies a systematic process for analyzing human performance gaps and for closing them.

title: Leading Change
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: An introduction to planning, implementing, and evaluating change efforts in people, teams, and organizations. Students will gain knowledge of how change models are used to strategically drive individual, team, and organizational outcomes.

title: Positive Psychology and Leadership in Organizations
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is designed to orient students to the use of positive psychology and authentic leadership to promote healthier, productive, and positive workplaces and organizations.

title: Major Learning Theories for the Adult Learner
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Through this course, learners engage with major paradigms of learning as they apply to adult learners based on the needs and problems faced by adult learners in adult learning contexts (I.e., the workplace). Topics covered in this class include behaviorism, cognitivism, and socio-cultural learning theories. Practical application in the design and implementation of learning opportunities for adult learners are key components of this course.

title: Transfer, Motivation and Metacognition for the Adult Learner
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is an extension of the previous course on major paradigms of learning as they apply to adult learners based on the needs and problems faced by adult learners in adult learning contexts (I.e., the workplace). Topics covered in the class include motivation, transfer, metacognition, and transformational learning theory. Practical application in the design and implementation of learning opportunities for adult learners are key components of this course.

title: Ethics in Design and Decision Making
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course fosters reflective practice on technology's impact on learning and performance. It explores ethics, systems theory, and cultural studies to guide the design, selection, and implementation of educational innovations.

title: Research Foundation in Social and Learning Sciences
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is designed to help students learning how to read and make sense of research reports by introducing the research process. Key topics include purpose statements, literature review, and quantitative and qualitative methods.

title: Assessment for Learning and Performance
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course covers assessment in learning and workplace systems, focusing on formative and summative assessments, feedback practices, competency-based learning, collaborative learning, learning analytics, and practical application in adult learning contexts.

title: Graduate Teaching I
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Introduces new Teaching and Graduate Assistants to teaching at UNM, reviews various instructional methods, assessment strategies, and pedagogical theories pertinent to teaching in higher education.

title: Problems
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

title: Workshop
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Special offerings given on demand for terms less than a semester. May be repeated to a maximum of 5 credit hours for Masters Plan I and a maximum of 8 credit hours for Masters Plan II.

title: Topics
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Used to test new courses.

title: Field Experiences
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This independent study is for students to gain experiences in settings other than those in which they are employed or who are making career transitions and would benefit from shadowing a professional in the field. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Internship
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This final independent study is the capstone experience for Master s students who opt not to do a thesis. The student submits a proposal for a minimum 200-hour project to his/her internship faculty supervisor. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Capstone
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description:
This course is designed to support students in the M.A. program to plan, implement, and evaluate an applied internship and portfolio as the culmination of their degree.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Directed Readings in Organization, Information, and Learning Sciences
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Student will develop an Individual Performance Contract with a faculty member to determine the key readings and will produce a product.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Science, Technology and Society
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Defines science, technology, human values and examines the impacts and relationships among them. Discusses emerging scientific and technological developments, projects effects on society and the proposition that technology is a primary determinant of social change.

title: Advanced Instructional Design
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: A theory-driven and project-based doctoral level seminar on the foundations of learning environments, instructional design theory, and the instructional design process. Students develop design models based on constructivist and socioconstructivist theories for innovative learning environments.

title: Current Research Methods for the Study of Learning
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Students learn current research methods for understanding learning as process. The focal method varies by semester. Students gain understanding of the research method, begin their own work, and apply the method.

title: Advanced Seminar in Organizational and Program Evaluation
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course is for students who wish to gain an in-depth understanding of evaluation theories and philosophies. In seminar format, students will study evaluation as a trans-discipline and its role in contemporary organizations.

title: Research in Online Education
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Advanced doctoral seminar on research in online education and educational telecommunications. Students will critically examine current research and develop theoretical frameworks, appropriate methodologies, a research proposal and an agenda for future online education research.

title: Advanced Instructional Technology Seminar
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This seminar emphasized the process of applying research findings to create innovative computer-based solutions for organizational learning problems. Steps in the process include assessing organizational learning needs, designing and implementing solutions and applying formative evaluation techniques.

title: Advanced Seminar on Organization Development and Consulting
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This advanced course in OD for doctoral students and advanced master s is designed to enable students to develop theoretical perspectives, intensive practice and understanding of the use of OD in improving organizations.

title: Advanced Seminar in Organizational Leadership
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This course provides an overview of leadership including its evolution, approaches and theories, women and leadership, culture and leadership, and leadership ethics. Students will develop an in depth understanding and a personal philosophy of leadership.

title: Dissertation Proposal Seminar
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: This seminar is the capstone course for the doctoral program. It assists students in planning and developing a dissertation proposal. Course may be repeated once. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Topics in Organization, Information, and Learning Sciences
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Topics in Organization, Information, and Learning Sciences. Restriction: admitted to OILS doctoral program.

title: Research Practicum
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description:
A faculty-supervised course culminating in a comprehensive paper or research proposal that integrates knowledge attained through coursework, research, and experience.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Directed Readings in Organization, Information, and Learning Sciences
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: A faculty-directed exploration of a specific topic through reading, discussion, and critique.

title: Dissertation
subject: Organization, Information, & Learning Sciences
description: Individual performance contract required between student and professor, following formal approval of dissertation committee. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Nonprofit Leadership and Practice
subject: Public Administration
description: This course examines the role that nonprofits play in addressing critical societal problems. This course explores the skills necessary to lead an effective and sustainable nonprofit organization. It investigates the best practices in community engagement. The course develops students’ capacity to respond to community needs and to develop relationships with community stakeholders.

title: Special Topics in Public Service
subject: Public Administration
description: Explore specific topics that address current issues related to the theory and/or practice of public service. Topics may include the role of public service in non-profit leadership and practice, ethics in public service, cross sector leadership, social entrepreneurship, and more.

title: Individual Study
subject: Public Administration
description: This course offers faculty-supervised individual study in an area of special interest not readily available through conventional course offerings. This course may focus on theory, specific contexts, and/or skills needed for the practice of public service.

title: Public Service Practicum
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course provides an experiential learning opportunity through placement with a public, private, or nonprofit organization. Students will use their first-hand involvement to better understand and more effectively communicate how they operate to serve a public need.
Restriction: permission of instructor

title: Introduction to Public Administration
subject: Public Administration
description: This seminar is an introductory-level graduate seminar introducing key concepts in public administration. It is designed as an introduction to the Public Administration curriculum, to key elements in government; to key issues in systems of governance, and to the multiple environments within which public administration professionals will work in the future, including the institutional, ideological, social and cultural environments.

title: Organizational Theory and Behavior
subject: Public Administration
description: This course introduces students to evidence-based management principles and covers a broad array of theories and conceptual models in the fields of organizational development and behavior. It provides analytic lenses through which students will develop strategic means to address ‘wicked problems’ that exist in public, healthcare and/or non-profit organizations.

title: Administration of State and Local Government
subject: Public Administration
description:
The organization, policies, processes and financing of state governments, cities, counties and special districts, with particular emphasis on human resources, budgets and planning.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Human Resources Management
subject: Public Administration
description: Survey of human resources management principles and practices in public, healthcare, and nonprofit organizations.

title: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion in the Public and Nonprofit Sectors.
subject: Public Administration
description:
The course covers the core dimensions, concepts, and approaches to diversity in organizations. Will consider the historical, political, cultural, and economic contexts as well as questions and controversies surrounding diversity management.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Administrative Law
subject: Public Administration
description:
Role and nature of administrative law; procedural requirements and judicial review of administrative actions; safeguards against arbitrary/capricious action; delegation of sovereignty and legislative power; legal principals in the development of public policy and administration.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Ethics in Public Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course aims to familiarize students with the ethical nature and dilemmas of American public administration. It looks at the ethical dilemmas and concerns that arise from the exercise of discretionary authority and administrative power.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Comparative Public Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
Examination on a comparative basis of national systems of administration in developed and developing countries, focusing on the organization and behavior of public bureaucracies, with special emphasis on Latin America. 
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Cross-Boundary Leadership and Governance
subject: Public Administration
description: This course focuses on the issue of cross-boundary governance, aiming to foster collaborative leadership across business, nonprofit and public sectors, tribal and other jurisdictions, and policy making and implementation systems. Cross-boundary competition and conflicts are often inevitable. How to manage them responsibly in governance is a central theme.

title: Non-Profit Governance
subject: Public Administration
description: This is an introductory course to the role and leadership of nonprofit organizations in sustainable development goals in the United States. This course will provide an overview of management skills required by leaders of nonprofit organizations, including nonprofit strategy, board governance, executive leadership, managing employees and volunteers, marketing, fundraising, social enterprise, and collaboration and competition among nonprofit organizations.

title: Financial Management for Public Organizations
subject: Public Administration
description: This course introduces students to budgeting concepts and models, financial control, reporting, and analysis. Topics also include management of public funds and contributions, expenditure controls, issues in financial administration, and the establishment of priorities through financial management. Students will also develop spreadsheet skills to perform financial calculations and create financial analysis reports.

title: Financial Management for Nonprofit Organizations
subject: Public Administration
description:
Course focuses on nonprofit financial decision-making, operating and capital budgeting, managing working capital, issues in implementing budgets and business plans, issues in government contracting with nonprofit organizations, and financial performance management.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Budgeting Systems
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course focuses on budgeting tools and techniques for public and/or healthcare organizations. Systems for planning and budgeting are critical to organizational survival and success. The course covers techniques for cash budgeting, operating budgeting, and capital budgeting. It addresses planning and budgetary processes, with specific attention paid to issues facing public and/or healthcare organizations.


Restriction: permission of department.

title: Problems
subject: Public Administration
description:
A topic relevant to public administration is developed, resulting in a paper of substantial length.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Professional Paper
subject: Public Administration
description:
Must be taken by all students who are not pursuing the thesis option. In general, papers will be more extensive than term papers, perhaps including case studies, reports of research results, theoretical essays or similar contributions of substantive and professional quality. Students must enroll for 3 hours the first semester, and then for 1 hour consecutively thereafter (including summer sessions), until their professional paper is approved. Only the first 3 credit hours will count toward the M.P.A. degree. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: MPA Practicum
subject: Public Administration
description: This course provides students with an opportunity to apply the concepts, strategies and tools acquired in a public or non-profit organization. Students with relevant professional experience may request a waiver.

title: Health Policy and Management
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course will examine critical issues currently facing health care managers and policy makers. Key areas of discussion are structure, financing and delivery of health services in the US.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Health Governance in Global Perspective
subject: Public Administration
description:
Seminar draws upon interdisciplinary perspectives in consideration and discussion of significant global health problems, ways concerned actors attempt to address them, and participants' own roles in improving health conditions. 
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Healthcare Finance
subject: Public Administration
description:
Health Finance helps students develop an understanding of the managerial aspects of financial analysis in health care organizations. It explores the concepts, principles and applications of financial management and decision-making in modern hospital and healthcare organization. 
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Health Care Quality Management
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course is designed for future leaders of health care organizations. The course provides students with the knowledge of how the best health care organizations deliver high quality and cost-effective health care services.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Health Economics
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course focuses on concepts and methods of analysis used in health economics, with a strong emphasis in healthcare evaluation and health policy decision-making, in particular its impact on patient care and healthcare delivery.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Health Care Ethics
subject: Public Administration
description:
The course is designed to prepare future health care leaders of health care organizations to deal with ethical issues and dilemmas. The course does not cover medical ethics, but focuses on management ethics.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Seminar on Environmental Policy and Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
Examination of issues and problems associated with the implementation of U.S. environmental policies and programs. Administration of natural resources on federal, state and local levels, with special reference to the Southwest.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Networking and Collaborative Governance for Public and Nonprofit Leadership
subject: Public Administration
description:
Complex policy problems defy traditional boundaries. The governance of inter-organizational and cross-sectoral networks is a crucial skill for effective leaders. Topics include network design, leadership, informal accountability, managing competition, innovation, social capital and network resilience.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Practice of Policy Development
subject: Public Administration
description:
Introduction to practice of policy development in technical and professional applications. Emphasis on writing, interpretation and implementation of policy documents. Environmental, physical and social policy are highlighted. 
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Topical Seminars
subject: Public Administration
description:
Seminars scheduled from time to time on issues and topics requiring additional focus in public administration. See course offerings each semester for seminars. 
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Research Design and Methods
subject: Public Administration
description: This course is designed to learn basic concepts and methods in public and/or health administration research. The course introduces main steps in the research process and provides basic knowledge and skills of research design. We will pay particular attention to important themes in research designs and methods focused on data collection/analysis techniques in quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods research.

title: Data Analysis for Decision Making
subject: Public Administration
description: This course focuses on data analysis prevalent in public administration, including descriptive and inferential statistics, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, correlation, cross-tabulation, mean comparison with significance testing, regression, ANOVA.

title: Program Evaluation
subject: Public Administration
description: This course is intended to provide an advanced introduction to the theory and practice of program evaluation, along with policy analysis and evaluation.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Public Administration
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Introduction to Healthcare Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course provides an overview of the evolving structure of the U.S. public health and health care delivery systems and is designed for graduate students in health policy and management.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Cultural Competence and Healthcare Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course will discuss the concept of culture: how it changes and how it influences everyday life, as well as health disparity, and what healthcare organizations/systems can do to implement strategies for enhancing cultural competence.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Healthcare Information Technology
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course is designed to help students develop a comprehensive understanding of the design, use, and evaluation issues and methodologies of health informatics applications.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Healthcare Payment Systems
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course focuses on the fundamentals of establishing compliance programs to identifiy and prevent fraud and abuse and familiarize students with various payment systems such as Medicare's prospective payment systems for hospitals and other provider reimbursements.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Hospital and Clinic Administration
subject: Public Administration
description:
This course is designed for future leaders of health care organizations. The course provides students with the knowledge about how the best health care organizations deliver high quality cost effective healthcare.
Restriciton: permission of department.

title: Practicum
subject: Public Administration
description:
M.H.A. practicums are typically offered mid-program, offering opportunities to apply program learning during the practicum experience and to bring practicum experience into the classroom. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: permission of department.

title: Capstone
subject: Public Administration
description: This course features analyses of selected public and healthcare administration cases. Students will apply what they have learned to real issues in public, nonprofit, and healthcare organizations and offer solutions to the challenges faced by administrative professionals.

title: Public Leadership for Social Change
subject: Public Administration
description: Addressing modern societal problems depends on the collaboration of key players from all levels of government, nonprofit organizations, commercial businesses and more. This course prepares students to contribute to improving social problems through a hands-on approach centered around the core theme of public leadership for social change.

title: PA Foundations of Research Methodology
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides an overview of Evidence-Based Practice, informatics, and clinically relevant statistics. It covers research design evaluation and introduces public health, health policy, and healthcare systems, preparing students for roles in public health and diverse patient care.

title: PA Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine I
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course is an introduction to care of children from birth through adolescence. Lectures emphasize ethics, age-appropriate physical examination and history-taking, growth and developmental milestones, preventive care and anticipatory guidance, dysmorphology, social determinants of health, hematology, fevers, and poisoning.

title: PA Human Anatomy
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides an overview of basic anatomical concepts, normal human anatomy, and embryology, with a focus on their relevance to clinical practice.

title: PA Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine II
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course focuses on the principles of care of children from birth through adolescence including cardiovascular, pulmonary, and renal conditions. This course has a primary care focus in alignment with the PA Program’s mission and goals.

title: PA Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine III
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides the PA student with the principles of care of children from birth through adolescence focusing on gastrointestinal conditions and nutrition. This course has a primary care focus in alignment with the PA Program’s mission and goals.

title: PA Adult and Geriatric Medicine I
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course equips PA students with essential knowledge and skills for primary care of adult and geriatric patients. It covers major biological principles, including anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and pathophysiology, and explores social, behavioral, and population perspectives.

title: PA Hematology
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides an overview of hematology, including hematopoiesis and hemostasis, and covers the pathophysiology, presentation, diagnosis, and management of common hematologic diseases.

title: PA Microbiology and Immunology
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course covers the human immune system, including innate, cellular, and humoral responses to infections, hypersensitivity, and autoimmune diseases. It also addresses fundamentals of infectious diseases, focusing on prevention, identification, and treatment of immunologic and infectious disorders.

title: PA Adult and Geriatric Medicine II
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course continues with principles of adult and geriatric health care, focusing on presentation, evaluation, and treatment of conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content for this age group.

title: PA Adult and Geriatric Medicine III
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course covers common primary care disorders in adult and geriatric patients, focusing on evaluation and management skills. It integrates with the current medical school block, emphasizing disease prevention, cultural issues, and chronic condition management.

title: PA Pharmacology I
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course introduces pharmacology and basic pharmacotherapeutics to first-year PA students. It emphasizes principles and mechanisms of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination (ADME), with a focus on clinical application in primary care.

title: PA Emergency Medicine I
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course introduces care in emergency departments and urgent care centers. It integrates with the current medical school block and emphasizes rapid evaluation and management of conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content.

title: PA Emergency Medicine II
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course continues education on care in emergency departments and urgent care centers. It integrates with the current medical school block and emphasizes rapid evaluation and management of conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content.

title: PA Pharmacology II
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course continues pharmacology and clinical pharmacotherapeutics for conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content. It builds on Pharmacology I principles, focusing on medication application and clinical use in primary care.

title: PA Pharmacology III
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course focuses on prototype drugs, including drug classes, generic names, organ system effects, metabolism, elimination, and drug interactions. It emphasizes the clinical application of these drugs for conditions covered in medical school content.

title: PA Emergency Medicine III
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course culminates education on care in emergency departments and urgent care centers. It integrates with the current medical school block and emphasizes rapid evaluation and management of conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content.

title: PA Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine IV
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course focuses on the principles of care of children from birth through adolescence focusing on neurological, psychiatric and behavioral disorders. This course has a primary care focus in alignment with the PA Program’s mission and goals.

title: PA Adult and Geriatric Medicine IV
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course focuses on adult and geriatric health care, emphasizing conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content. It develops problem-solving skills and compares care for adults and the elderly.

title: PA Clinical Skills I
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course, part of a series, teaches first-year PA students history taking, physical exams, and clinical reasoning. It includes lectures, practice sessions, and standardized patient experiences, fostering inter-professional understanding and teamwork.

title: PA Clinical Skills II
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course, part of a series, enhances first-year PA students' history taking, physical exam skills, and clinical reasoning. It includes clinical skills sessions, practice, and standardized patient experiences, and introduces the series of clinic exposures with Continuity Clinic 1.

title: PA Clinical Skills III
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course builds on prior Clinical Skills, including competency exams in organ system content from medical school, and includes a half-day per week clinical experience.

title: PA Pharmacology IV
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course continues pharmacology and clinical pharmacotherapeutics, applying principles from Pharmacology I to medications for conditions related to the organ system covered in medical school content. It emphasizes clinical application and drug use in primary care.

title: PA Clinical Skills IV
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course, part of a series, helps second-year PA students refine history-taking, physical exam skills, clinical reasoning, and oral presentations, preparing them for clinical year clerkships and the Final Summative Exam.

title: PA Clinical Seminar
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course introduces the Physician Assistant profession, covering anatomy, physiology, and population health topics such as epidemiology, health promotion, disease prevention, health policy, and models for change, with a focus on rural health in New Mexico.

title: PA Dermatology
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course covers major biological principles of dermatology, including anatomy, normal physiology, pharmacology, and pathophysiology.

title: PA Orthopedics
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course introduces students to common disorders of the musculoskeletal system via a mix of lectures, small group clinical case work, and hands-on workshops.  Students practice orthopedic physical exam maneuvers and interpret skeletal radiographs and other imagining modalities as applicable.

title: PA Neurosciences
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides a foundation in the basic medical and clinical science of the nervous system, with a focus on neurology, psychiatry, and behavioral medicine.

title: PA CV-Pulmonary-Renal
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides a foundation in the basic medical sciences of the cardiovascular, pulmonary, and renal systems, covering physiology, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and pharmacotherapeutics associated with common disorders of these organ systems.

title: PA Infectious Disease
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides an overview of the medical and clinical science of human infectious diseases, including viral, bacterial, fungal, and parasitic conditions. Emphasis is on preventing, identifying, and treating infectious disorders commonly seen by physician assistants.

title: PA GI, Nutrition, Metabolism (GINM)
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides basic medical and clinical foundations of the gastrointestinal (GI) system, nutrition, and metabolism (NM), including pathophysiology associated with common disorders. It emphasizes a primary care focus, aligning with the PA Program’s mission and goals.

title: PA Sexuality, Reproduction and Endocrine
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides a foundation in the basic medical and clinical science of human sexuality, the human reproductive system, and the endocrine system, including the pathophysiology associated with common disorders of these organ systems.

title: PA Clerkship Family Medicine
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship is a first-year field experience covering the healthcare needs of patients across the lifespan, with a focus on major aspects of primary health care.

title: PA Clerkship Women's Health and Prenatal Care
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship focuses on managing women’s health care in a family practice setting, including evaluation and management of common gynecological conditions and routine prenatal care.

title: PA Clerkship Pediatrics
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship in family practice-pediatrics focuses on developing skills in the healthcare of pediatric and adolescent patients.

title: PA Clerkship Behavioral Medicine - Psychiatry
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship focuses on the healthcare of patients with behavioral health issues commonly seen in primary care. Field experience includes both office and clinic/inpatient settings.

title: PA Clerkship Emergency Medicine
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship focuses on the triage, evaluation, and management of patients in the emergency setting.

title: PA Clerkship General Internal Medicine
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship focuses on the care of adult patients in both outpatient and inpatient settings, providing a foundation for subspecialty courses such as cardiology and endocrinology.

title: PA Clerkship Elective
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship offers students the opportunity to select a clinical field experience in an area of personal interest.

title: PA Clerkship Surgery
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship focuses on the care of surgical patients, including operating room experience, pre- and post-operative care, and patient assessment in office and inpatient settings.

title: PA Foundations of Medical Science
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course provides an overview of cellular and molecular function, genetic physiology and pathophysiology, and introduces pharmacology.

title: PA Clerkship Primary Care
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This supervised clerkship integrates elements from Family Practice and specialty clerkships, enabling students to advance their clinical management skills and function at a higher level in patient care.

title: PA Program to Practice
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: This course allows students to demonstrate skills from the PA curriculum and readiness for the profession. It includes instruction on PA competencies, lectures, small group seminars, and a HRSA community health project using the PDSA cycle method.

title: Independent Study
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: The Physician Assistant Independent Study course allows students to focus on personalized areas of interest or challenge. Students develop tailored study plans with faculty, covering advanced topics or research, with regular evaluations to ensure alignment with PA program competencies.

title: Topics
subject: Physician Assistant Studies
description: The Physician Assistant Topics course addresses curricular needs essential for institutional and accreditation standards. It offers a comprehensive, adaptable curriculum, ensuring students are well-prepared for the requirements of their training and future professional practice.

title: Topics in Peace Studies
subject: Peace Studies
description: Current topics in Peace Studies to be explored in experimental courses.

title: Peace Studies Internship
subject: Peace Studies
description:
Placement in community-based organization active in conflict resolution, peacemaking, and/or social justice. Arranged by student in consultation with advisor. Must be supervised by a faculty member.  
Restriction: junior or senior standing, and permission of Peace Studies advisor and internship instructor.

title: Introduction to Peace Studies
subject: Peace Studies
description: Introduction to peace research.  Primary content of Peace Studies program; focuses on the concepts of peace/war, security/ conflict, and violence/non-violence.  Special emphasis on non-violent conflict resolution, human rights, and social justice issues.

title: Cardio Kickboxing
subject: Physical Education (Non-Professional)
description: A multi dimensional fitness program that is incorporated in kicking and boxing skills.

title: Walk For Wellness
subject: Physical Education (Non-Professional)
description: Designed to introduce the basic fundamentals of personal fitness. The workout will consist of correct posture, arm swing, stride and pace which will lower the risk of injury. The topics covered are the following principles of fitness, health related and motor skill related components of fitness, weight control, common fitness injuries and stress management.

title: Martial Arts
subject: Physical Education (Non-Professional)
description: Students will be introduced to Martial Arts styles including Tae Kwon Do, Kenpo, Jiu-Jitsu, Aikido concepts, wrestling, boxing and others.

title: Physical Education in Secondary Schools
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Curriculum and pedagogy for effective physical education in secondary schools. Pre-requisites: PEP 319.

title: Teaching Exercise
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
An overview of the educational concepts, performance techniques, program design and leadership skills needed to teach group exercise. The course will include analysis and application of effective exercise procedures for all fitness levels.
Prerequisite: 326L and PRPE 2165.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Exercise Science.

title: Physical Education in the Elementary School
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Curriculum and pedagogy for effective elementary physical education. Pre-requisites: PRPE 2120, PRPE 2125, PRPE 2170, PRPE 2175

title: Fundamentals of Exercise Physiology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Study of the immediate and long-term effects of exercise on physiological systems of the human body. 
Prerequisite: BIOL 2210 and BIOL 2210L.

title: Clinical Exercise in Physical Therapy Online
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This online course addresses physiological effects of exercise related to systems of the body with emphasis on the cardiopulmonary and neuromuscular systems. We apply these principles for designing specialized exercise programs for effective patient care.
Prerequisite: BIOL 2210 and BIOL 2225.

title: General Medical Conditions in Athletic Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is designed to provide information relative to general medical conditions. Emphasis will be placed on the etiology, development and treatment of pathophysiological processes.
Prerequisite: 481 and PRPE 2145.

title: Therapeutic Modalities
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is designed to provide information relative to the physiological principles and operational procedures of contemporary therapeutic modalities as they relate to the care and treatment of athletic injuries.
Prerequisite: PRPE 2145.

title: Pharmacology in Athletic Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is designed to provide the athletic training student with an understanding of pharmacological applications and governing pharmacy regulations relevant to athletic training.
Prerequisite: 374.

title: Problems
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Student Teaching in the Elementary School
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is for teacher candidates entering the elementary student teaching practicum. Pre-requisites: PEP 301, PEP 319

title: Assessment in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provide physical education students the ability to select, design, and implement performance-based assessment.

title: Classroom and Behavior Management in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provide physical education students with strategies and techniques for effective classroom/behavior management.

title: Teaching and Learning in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Theories and concepts related to teaching physical education.

title: Student Teaching in the Secondary Schools
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Student teaching in secondary schools. Pre-requisites: PEP 301, PEP 319.

title: Adapted Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: The field of adaptive and corrective physical education and its relationship to the regular curriculum in PE.

title: Physical Disabilities and Causes
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Investigation of etiology, characteristics and treatment appropriate for individuals with physical disabilities who are in public sector, schools and exercise programs.

title: Management Concepts in Sport and Fitness Settings
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed to prepare prospective managers, directors and program coordinators for sport and fitness settings. Human relations and management skills will be emphasized.

title: Designs for Fitness
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Focuses on physical fitness assessment and exercise prescription and includes 1) use of field tests and laboratory tests to appraise physical fitness levels; 2) designs of individualized physical fitness programs; and 3) evaluation of exercise programs. 
Prerequisite: 326L and PRPE 2155 and PRPE 2165.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Exercise Science.

title: Exercise and Disease Prevention
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Identification and analysis of current disease prevention issues related to exercise, physical activity and lifestyle.  
Prerequisite: 326L and PRPE 2165. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Exercise Science.

title: Rehabilitation of Athletic Injuries
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Designed to provide the athletic training student with the basic components of a comprehensive rehabilitation program, therapeutic goals, modalities and exercise, progression criteria and methods of evaluating/re-evaluating and recording rehabilitation progress.  
Prerequisite: 374 and BIOL 2210 and BIOL 2210L and BIOL 2225 and BIOL 2225L and PRPE 2135 and PRPE 2145 and PRPE 2165.

title: Athletic Training Administration
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
The student will learn to plan, coordinate and supervise administrative components of an athletic training program for a high school, college or professional athletic organization.  
Prerequisite: 374 and 481.

title: EKG Interpretation
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Anatomical and physiological approach to the interpretation of resting 12-lead electrocardiograms. Course fee.

title: Exercise Testing and Interpretation
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Practical and theoretical skills necessary to safely conduct graded exercise tests on treadmills and ergometers.

title: Sports Physiology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
The student will learn to properly analyze any sport in terms of specific conditioning demands and be able to design a training prescription for any sport.  
Prerequisite: 326L and PRPE 2165. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Exercise Science.

title: Organization and Administration of Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Program building, including criteria for the selection of activities and progression, and other factors affecting course of study such as facilities, equipment, budget, laws, policies, professional responsibilities.

title: Principles of Coaching
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course consists of an in-depth study of the coaching profession, helping students develop an understanding of the nature of the profession and its inherent responsibilities.

title: Athletic Training Clinical II
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Provide an introduction to basic clinical skills used in the professional activities of the athletic trainer. Fieldwork in the athletic training room is included. Minimum of 200 clinical hours.
Prerequisite: PRPE 2145.

title: Athletic Training Clinical III
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provide the athletic training student with an opportunity to apply clinical skills. The athletic training student gains practical experience through assignment to an approved clinical instructor. Minimum of 200 clinical hours. Prerequisite: 481.

title: Ergogenic Aids for Sport Performance
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: The use of ergogenic aids, whether pharmacological, technological or psychological is widely used in sport. This course will focus on identifying and exploring the effects of researched ergogenic aids.

title: Athletic Training Clinical IV
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provides the opportunity to apply clinical skills and gain field experience through assignment to an off-campus high school and/or clinic setting. Minimum of 200 clinical hours. Prerequisite: 483.

title: Research in Athletic Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is designed to examine evidence-based practice, patient outcomes and research in the field of athletic training.
Prerequisite: 375 and 473 and 483 and PRPE 2140.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Athletic Training.

title: Topics in Athletic Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is designed to examine current topics, career development, practice analysis and transition to practice in the field of athletic training.
Prerequisite: 375 and 473 and 483 and PRPE 2140.

title: Topics
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: A course exploring a topic not covered by the standard curriculum but of interest to faculty and students in a particular semester.

title: Practicum
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Planned and supervised professional laboratory or field experiences in agency or institutional setting.  Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Exercise Science Senior Seminar
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
A capstone for Exercise Science students in their last semester of the program. The course bridges the gap between undergraduate education and Exercise Science research.

Restriction: Exercise Science students in the last semester of program.

title: Emergent Response in Athletic Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Best practices to manage traumatic injuries, respiratory and circulatory arrest, and acute illness will be presented, discussed, and practices as outlined in the educational competencies set by the National Athletic Trainers' Association Board of Certification.
Prerequisite: PRPE 2110 and PRPE 2130 and PRPE 2135 and PRPE 2140 and PRPE 2145.

title: Exercise Science Seminar
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Designed to orient students to Exercise Science graduate programs and serves as a forum for exchange of research in the field.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Specific topics of interest to those who need an introduction to the practice of exercise physiology and to become familiar with research possibilities and career opportunities in the field of exercise physiology.

title: Designs for Fitness
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Focuses on physical fitness assessment and exercise prescription and includes 1) use of field tests and laboratory tests to appraise physical fitness levels; 2) designs of individualized physical fitness programs; and 3) evaluation of exercise programs.

title: EKG Interpretation
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Anatomical and physiological approach to the interpretation of resting 12-lead electrocardiograms. Course fee.

title: Research Design in HPER
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Emphasizes an understanding of different research designs, their level of sophistication and their application from both a theoretical and practical point of view.

title: Exercise Testing and Interpretation
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Practical and theoretical skills necessary to safely conduct graded exercise tests on treadmills and ergometers. Prerequisite: 502 and 503.

title: Curriculum Construction in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Designed for those individuals engaged in curriculum development and revision. Theoretical and practical application for construction of physical education courses/programs.

title: Seminar in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: The course covers current topics, trends and issues in physical education and sport.

title: Metabolic Considerations of Exercise Science
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: An advanced study of the methodology, techniques and applications of biochemistry research as it applies to metabolic aspects of exercise and nutritional biochemistry.

title: Laboratory Procedures and Instrumentation in Applied Physiology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Use of all routine testing procedures and instrumentation in the Center for Exercise Laboratory. Requires considerable extra-class independent work in the laboratory. Completion of this course is mandatory for any student planning to use the laboratory facilities.

title: Body Composition
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Covers theoretical and applied aspects of body composition assessment. Students critically analyze currently used and newly developed laboratory and field techniques for evaluating body composition.

title: Introduction to Sport Administration
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provides the opportunity for students interested in pursuing a career in the broad field of sport administration to identify the skills, knowledge and experiences needed by managers of sport programs. Analyze potential career opportunities.

title: Sport Sociology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Investigates: a) the reciprocal impact of sport on society; b) individual and group behavior as influenced by social relationships within social settings; and c) the multiple roles of sport in cross-cultural contexts.

title: Ethics in Sport and Fitness
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Designed to promote critical self-evaluation, examine one's philosophy/values, refine moral reasoning skills and study moral/ethical issues in sport and exercise environments.

title: Physiology of Resistance Training
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
This course is intended to be an advanced study of the tissue and systems research published on acute and chronic physiological adaptations known to occur with resistance training.
Restriction: admitted to M.S. Physical Education or Ph.D. Physical Education, Sports and Exercise Science.

title: Sport Leadership
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Study of leadership theory and its application to the effective administration of sport programs. Course also examines current sport leadership research as well as the governance of amateur and professional sport organizations.

title: Sport Marketing and Promotions
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: A study of the current approaches sport managers utilize for conducting relationships with consumers in sport environments. The course will focus on evaluation of sport sponsorships, promotional strategies and development of a marketing plan.

title: Financing Sport
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: A study of the approaches sport managers utilize for acquiring revenue and managing funds in sport environments. The course will focus on economic impact studies, public subsidization of sport facilities and innovative revenue acquisition strategies.

title: Risk Management in Sport
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course will focus primarily on one practical aspect of sport law and sport management, that of liability, safety and risk management. The course is designed to help teachers, coaches, facility managers, program directors, etc. develop the knowledge and skills to recognize and eliminate dangerous situations before they become a problem.

title: Exercise in Extreme Environment
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Classic and recent published research is used to explore the altered exercise-related human physiology during human exposure to our main environmental stressors-altitude/ hypoxia, heat/dehydration, positive g-forces and microgravity.

title: Legal Aspects of Sports
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: A study of selected areas of the law and how they relate to the world of sports, physical activity, physical education and recreation. An emphasis will be placed on current issues and practical applications.

title: The Analysis of Teaching Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Investigates education in contemporary society, examines theories and styles of teaching, reviews research related to teaching, studies methods for determining teacher effectiveness and discusses other topics related to teaching physical education.

title: Assessment and Data Literacy in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course provides graduate students with an enhanced understanding of data driven decision making, data literacy, and assessment as related to standards-based curriculum development in physical education.

title: Sport Facilities Planning and Construction
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course provides an overview of the fundamentals of planning, design and construction of athletic, physical education, recreation and sport facilities and the relationship of facilities to programs.

title: Sport Event Management
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provides students with the knowledge, skills and understanding necessary to propose, develop and conduct sport-related contests and special events. Also covers elements of facility and game management.

title: Sports Physiology
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: The student will learn to properly analyze any sport in terms of specific conditioning demands and be able to design a training prescription for any sport.

title: Principles of Coaching
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course consists of an in-depth study of the coaching profession, helping students develop an understanding of the nature of the profession and its inherent responsibilities.

title: Sociopolitical Issues in Teaching Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Presents an introduction to sociopolitical issues in teaching and teacher socialization and varying perspectives surrounding the study of how teachers adopt the values, skills, knowledge, and cultural norms of the profession of teaching.

title: Readings in Physical Education Teacher Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provides an introduction to research in physical education teacher education. Readings, discussion, and writings serve to deepen understanding literature and guide students to identifying an area of interest for their capstone project, thesis, or dissertation.

title: Supervision of Physical Education Programs
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Designed to examine supervisory theory and research to help students acquire an understanding of all the areas supervision in physical education encompasses and to assist the student to develop specific supervisory skills.

Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Advanced Field Experiences
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Practical experience in a public, private or non-profit organization, supervised by a professional with an academic component overseen by a UNM instructor.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Directed Readings in Physical Education
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: A faculty-directed exploration of a specific topic through reading, discussion, and critique.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Dissertation Seminar
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed to assist doctoral students in the preparation and writing of their dissertation proposal. Students focus their research project, and prepare their draft dissertation proposal and PowerPoint presentation.

title: Special Topics in Sport Pedagogy
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed to present graduate students with the most innovative research trends and topics in sport pedagogy and PETE. Topics and content for the course are different with each iteration and are the discretion of the faculty member serving as the instructor of record.

title: Social Justice in Physical Activity and Sport
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed for graduate students to deeply examine the literature and discussion surrounding sociocultural perspectives and issues, critical pedagogies, and their specific implementation in physical education, physical activity, and sport contexts.

title: Administration of PETE Programs
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed for graduate students to engage in applied and research-driven discussions and practice implementing a physical education teacher education program.

title: Pedagogy Research Laboratory
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course is designed for graduate students to gain practical experience in empirical research in physical education teacher education within the context of a collaborative research group.

title: Using Theory in Kinesiology Research
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course will present graduate students with select theoretical frameworks that are commonly used in sport pedagogy research and how to utilize them in designing rigorous studies that are grounded in theory.

title: Organizational Theory in Sport
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Examines current research related to organizational study in amateur, professional and commercial sport. Requires analysis of topic related to sport organization goals and effectiveness, structure, strategy, change, politics and organizational culture.

title: Sport Consumer Behavior
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: This course will compare and contrast the various research methodologies most commonly practiced in sport marketing settings. Through systematic analysis of the sport marketing mix, students will demonstrate proficiency in conducting and presenting sport market research.

title: Seminar in Sport Research
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Provides an understanding of the foundational research and literature in Sport Administration. An in-depth literature review of a selected topic will be conducted and future research questions will be identified.

title: Writing for Professional Publication
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Designed to guide the student through the process of writing, organizing, illustrating and submitting scientific papers for publication in scholarly journals.

title: Professional Considerations for Exercise Science
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: Latest research on specific topics of present interest is synthesized, presented and discussed. Course requires independent work, active participation in class discussions and advanced standing in exercise physiology.

title: Cellular and Molecular Considerations of Exercise Science
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description: An advanced study of methodology, techniques and applications of biochemistry research applicable to exercise science. Emphasis will be placed on many of the applied and molecular aspects in research.

Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

Restriction: permission of instructor.
