A faculty-directed exploration of a specific topic through reading, discussion, and critique.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Dissertation
subject: Physical Education (Professional)
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a doctoral dissertation.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Introduction to Population Health
subject: Public Health
description: Introduction to Population Health provides a population perspective on the multi-level (ecologic) determinants of health, disease and injury; the programs, policies and services that protect and promote health and prevent disease; and the analytic tools used by population health professionals.

title: Global Health Challenges and Responses
subject: Public Health
description: Global health is concerned with developing theories and methods to understand the roots of social, economic, political and environmental determinants of health, with a focus on the nature of health inequalities across the world.

title: Introduction to Community Health Work
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an overview of history and introduction to the profession, including scope of practice, roles, competencies, attributes and qualities. It provides practice-based guidelines for professional conduct, ethics and boundaries, confidentiality and informed consent.

title: Fundamentals of One Health
subject: Public Health
description: Introduction to One Health and its collaborative approach to design and implement research programs, policies and legislation that covers multiple sectors to achieve better health outcomes which includes: Introduction to biological disease basis, including cellular, physiological, genetic, immunologic, and environmental determinants. Pathologic mechanisms and host susceptibility for infectious and non-infectious diseases of population health importance including disease prevention/control delivered in a team-based format.

title: Community Health Work: Frameworks, Principles, and Practices for Direct Service
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides a broad introduction to public health as the framework for providing direct services to individuals, with focus on the ecological model, health equity, and healthcare systems.

title: Health Coaching and Health Promotion
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides a strong foundation in health coaching and health promotion. It offers strategies and skills for supporting behavior change including action planning, motivational interviewing, and communication skills.

title: Health Navigation and Service Coordination
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an overview of models, skills, tools, resources, and considerations for providing strengths-based health navigation and service coordination with clients.

title: Health Education and Facilitation
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an overview of the major approaches, models, skills, and knowledge needed to plan, facilitate, and evaluate basic health education presentations for groups in clinical and community settings.

title: Community Health Outreach, Assessment and Advocacy
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an overview of various approaches, models, methods, and considerations for conducting home visiting, health outreach, community organizing, and advocacy for improving community health.

title: Population Health: Introduction to Social, Cultural, Behavioral Theory
subject: Public Health
description:
Examine and apply social, cultural, and behavioral theories and models that inform and strengthen population health practice. Theories are used to diagnose health and social problems and plan interventions to improve the public's health.

Prerequisite: 101 and 102.

title: Introduction to Environmental and Occupational Health
subject: Public Health
description:
Environmental and occupational health and safety; including regulatory processes, compliance, pollution prevention, drinking water, wastewater management, solid/hazardous waste, air quality, food protection, zoonotic and vector-borne disease control, radiation, injury prevention.
Prerequisite: 101 and 102.

title: Health Systems, Services and Policies
subject: Public Health
description:
Increase the analytical capacity and critical thinking in regards to the US health system, services and related policies. Reinforce the students' sense of social responsibility and further their understanding of population health approaches. 
Prerequisite: 101 and 102.

title: Fundamentals of Health Care Finance
subject: Public Health
description:
This course will introduce basic concepts of health care finance: access, affordability, quality, and portability.
Prerequisite: 101 and 102.

title: Special Topics
subject: Public Health
description: Topics in population health that are not covered in the existing curriculum that are mutually agreed upon by students and faculty. May be repeated for credit provided the subject matter varies.

title: Population Health Research Methods
subject: Public Health
description:
Foundational understanding of scientific paradigms, approaches, methods and designs on population health research; definitions of health research problems at population, community, social group, system and service levels; ethical procedures.
Prerequisite: 201 and 221 and 230 and 240 and 241 and 311.

title: Essentials of Epidemiology: The Language of Population Health
subject: Public Health
description:
Introduction to analytic tools and methods used to quantify population health problems. Epidemiologists monitor, quantify and map disease, and critically assess the impact of medical treatments and population health interventions.
Prerequisite: MATH 1350.

title: Health Data Systems
subject: Public Health
description:
Introduces population health data systems in clinical and public health settings including electronic health records, data standards, legal aspects of health information, coding, and reimbursement. Big healthcare data sources will be explored.
Prerequisite: 201 and 221 and 230 and 240 and 241 and 311.

title: Population Health Management
subject: Public Health
description:
Examine policies and interventions regarding population health outcomes. Methods to predict patient risk and engagement. Quality and safety strategies and benchmarks, and information technology for use in population health management decision support.

Prerequisite: 221 and 311.

title: Population Health Evidenced-Based Practices
subject: Public Health
description:
Introduces students to core concepts in population-based primary and secondary prevention strategies for population health issues. Students will critically examine evidence-based guidelines used to informed population health interventions.

Prerequisite: 221.

title: Assessment and Planning
subject: Public Health
description:
Describe and apply assessment and planning processes to determine priorities for population health interventions. Provide overview of planning and development of population health interventions from a systems perspective, with attention to evidence-based, theoretical, ethical approaches.
Prerequisite: 420.

title: Program Evaluation
subject: Public Health
description:
Describe and apply the implementation/management and evaluation processes for population health interventions. Provides an overview of the implementation and evaluation of population health interventions from a systems perspective.
Prerequisite: 421.

title: Special Topics in Population Health
subject: Public Health
description: Variable topics in population health provides students to work with faculty on topics that are not part of the curriculum.

title: Introduction to Maternal and Child Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: This course focuses on the public health concepts related to determinants of health status and health disparities; behavioral, cultural, social, and political theories of disease and health inequities; prevention and health promotion; community-based interventions; and health policy.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar I
subject: Public Health
description: This seminar focuses on the description and history of Maternal and Child Health programs, Title V programs (national and state), the populations served by Title V programs along with their specific needs, the life course perspective, and the developmental cycles.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar II
subject: Public Health
description: This course focuses on career paths and the variety of professions working in maternal child health, policy initiatives in maternal child health on the national, state and local level, and evidence-based research on best practices in maternal child health programs.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar III
subject: Public Health
description: MCH Seminar focuses on MCH in local communities.  Because New Mexico is primarily a rural/ frontier state with many diverse communities and high rates of poverty and Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), this seminar will focus on the needs of communities, the services available, and the challenges involved in receiving services.

title: Population Health Capstone
subject: Public Health
description:
Provides an opportunity to earn credit hours (1-class, 5-field) through an experiential population health issue in a clinical or public health venue. This facilitates integration of classroom learning and practical experience during the Capstone.

Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

Prerequisite: 421.

title: Population Health Independent Study
subject: Public Health
description:
Students work individually with faculty members on projects with individual supervision.
Prerequisite: 101 and 102.
Restriction: permission of advisor.

title: Determinants and Equity in Public Health
subject: Public Health
description:
Concepts of public health related to determinants of health; cultural, social and political concepts of disease; disease prevention; health promotion, including individual behavior change and community based intervention; health policy. 
Restriction: admitted to M.P.H. Public Health.

title: Introduction to Epidemiology Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: Introduction to Epidemiology (PH 502) is an introduction to the basic epidemiologic methods used in population and public health.  This is a graduate level course intended for Master of Public Health students and others who would like to learn epidemiologic concepts and study designs in public health.  For those planning to participate in the epidemiology concentration of the MPH, this course serves as a prerequisite for additional advanced courses. Students are required to achieve a B or better in in this course and the Introduction to Biostatistics course (PH 536) to enroll in the next sequence of advanced courses (Advanced Epidemiology and Advanced Biostatistics).

title: Environmental-Occupational Health
subject: Public Health
description: Applies the public health perspective to environmental and occupational disease. Students will learn to apply the ecologic principles of agent, host and environment to diseases associated with exposures to the physical environment and chemical contaminants.

title: Health Care Systems
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an overview of the US health system and the main policies that shaped it, including the complex infrastructure of public health and the health care system, analyzing their historical development, organization, financing, and delivery of services; its performance compared to other health care systems; the key interest groups that shape the health policies; and the main policy challenges, scenarios for improvement, and proposals for change.

title: Public Health and Health Care Management
subject: Public Health
description: This course will focus on the core functions of public health and healthcare management and the leadership and management skills needed to achieve defined goals of public health programs. The role and elements of professionalism and ethics will be integrated throughout the course.

title: Global Health
subject: Public Health
description: This master’s level course provides an overview of the core topics and perspectives on global health, including the global conditions and structural determinants of health, the policies that shaped the field, the governance and cooperation systems, and the complex itinerary of the health systems in high and LMIC.

title: Public Health Seminar
subject: Public Health
description: A graduate seminar and journal club focusing on a wide range of PH topics. Speakers present original research. Journal club guides students to critically assess literature. Two semesters required for credit.

title: Social Epidemiology
subject: Public Health
description:
Social Epidemiology provides students with principles and methods of design, conduct analysis, and interpretation of epidemiologic research using a social epidemiology approach.
Prerequisite: 502 with a grade of "B" or better. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
subject: Public Health
description: Learn basic epidemiological principles of infectious diseases. Learn and understand the multiple factors associated with spread of infectious agents within populations and development, application and evaluation of control measures to stop or prevent transmission.

title: Perinatal Epidemiology
subject: Public Health
description: Review of a wide range of topics central to perinatal epidemiology. Highlighted topics will include conception and early fetal loss, design issues in studies of adverse reproductive outcomes and epidemiologic aspects and public health approaches to prevention of congenital malformation.

title: Public Health Research Methods
subject: Public Health
description: Quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods of applying and understanding the scientific inquiry used in health and social sciences research. Identify health-related problems and formulate questions that can be translated into sound research designs.

title: Epidemiology Data Analysis
subject: Public Health
description: Students will learn how to conduct a careful epidemiologic data analysis. The focus of the course is developing the practical and critical thinking skills to conduct an epidemiologic data analysis. This course is required for epidemiology concentration students.

title: Introduction to Biostatistics in Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: This course provides an introduction to biostatistics with a focus on its application in public health. Topics covered include random events, basic probability theory, sampling, estimation, hypothesis testing, categorical data analysis, nonparametric tests, correlation, simple linear regression, and One-Way ANOVA. Emphasis is placed on understanding statistical concepts and their practical implementation in public health research and practice.

title: Advanced Epidemiology Methods
subject: Public Health
description: This course is designed to provide students with a greater depth of knowledge of the principles and methods central to the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of epidemiologic work.

title: Epidemiology and Biostatistics Lab
subject: Public Health
description: Covers basic statistical methods, including statistical summaries and inference. Methods of summarizing data include graphical displays and numerical summaries. Statistical inference includes hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Methods for continuous and categorical data are studied.

title: Advanced Biostatistics
subject: Public Health
description: Covers basic models used in the statistical analysis of studies in the medical sciences and public health field, with an emphasis on epidemiology. Linear regression, analysis of variance, logistic regression, and survival models are studied.

title: Interventions for Health Equity
subject: Public Health
description: An exploration of rational health planning methods. Methods will be applied in the development of a health program plan within a social context where public health planning actually occurs. Involves the development of a realistic program plan addressing a health-related problem and writing a proposal for funding.

title: Health Policy, Politics and Social Equity
subject: Public Health
description: Provides students with understanding of factors within and outside of health care system. Reviews social policy in addressing coverage of uninsured, improving population health and reducing social inequities. Examination of frameworks and politics of policy programs.

title: Public Health Evaluation Methods
subject: Public Health
description: Introduces students to the language and theory of program evaluation to undertake their own evaluation design: how to pose evaluation research questions; data collection methodologies available to them; how to make decisions about appropriate data collection methods for different types of evaluation objectives.

title: Community Participatory-Based Research
subject: Public Health
description: Presents historical background, underlying assumptions, principles and steps for conducting CBPR. Introduces indigenous and decolonizing theories and methodologies of CBPR. Develops perspective on roles of culture, race, gender, and power in academic-community research partnerships.

title: Intervention Research with Marginalized Populations
subject: Public Health
description: This course addresses intervention research methods and approaches that are more effective in addressing health and social needs of marginalized populations. Designed to provide an overview to fundamental public health conceptual and methodological considerations.

title: Special Topics in Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: A course exploring a topic not covered by the standard curriculum but of interest to faculty and students in a particular semester.

title: Welcome to the Frontline: essential Public Health Roles for MD's
subject: Public Health
description: This course will prepare medical students and residents for their essential roles in the public health system, including public health surveillance, vital data collection, emergency preparedness, and health policy and advocacy. Students will meet experts in each of these four areas and demonstrate competency in each essential role through completion of assessments and demonstrated proficiency in related core skill sets. During the semester, students will plan and present a 30-minute seminar or recruit an expert speaker to present a 30-minute seminar, on a topic of their choice related to one of the essential roles. Each student will also create a 4-6 page paper or a 1-2 page issue or policy brief. A rubric will be provided for the seminar assignment and writing assignments.

title: Public Health and Health Care Communication
subject: Public Health
description: Health communication is the study of how health information is generated and disseminated and how that information affects individuals, community groups, institutions and public policy.

title: Introduction to Maternal and Child Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: Introduction to Maternal & Child Public Health focuses on the public health concepts related to determinants of health status and health disparities; behavioral, cultural, social, and political theories of disease and health inequities; prevention and health promotion; community-based interventions; and health policy. It includes historical, theoretical, skills-based, and practical approaches using case examples drawn from major health and health dis-parities problems in New Mexico and the United States.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar I
subject: Public Health
description: The MCH Seminar I focuses on the description and history of MCH, Title V programs (national and state), populations served by Title V programs along with their specific needs, life course perspective, and developmental cycles.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar II
subject: Public Health
description: Maternal Child Health Seminar 2 focuses on career paths and the variety of professions working in maternal child health, policy initiatives on the national, state and local level and evidence-based research best practices.

title: Maternal Child Health Seminar III
subject: Public Health
description: This seminar focuses on MCH in local communities. The impacts of poverty on women, children and families will be examined through readings, webinars, trainings, videos, discussions, reflections, and guest lectures.

title: New Mexico Border Health: US - Mexico Border Migration and Latino Health
subject: Public Health
description: Gives students applied understanding of public health disparities, equity challenges, and assets in the US-Mexico border region. Community based learning via site visit to border region with Web-CT enhanced instruction.

title: Global Indigenous Health
subject: Public Health
description: Course integrates physical, cultural, social, political, intellectual and emotional wellbeing of Indigenous populations globally. It examines health as a collective and individual inter-generational continuum that links to health status, practices, data, equity, policy and systems.

title: Health Systems and Globalization
subject: Public Health
description:
This seminar will examine international health care systems to identify commonalities and unique differences in structure and outcomes. Particular attention will be directed toward the financing, payer structure, delivery system models, health care equity, and what can be transferred across international boundaries. In addition, the impact global factors on health care national schemes will also be discussed.  

Advisor permission required

title: Independent Studies
subject: Public Health
description: Students work individually with faculty members on projects with individual supervision.

title: Master of Public Health Culminating Experience
subject: Public Health
description: The Master of Public Health Culminating Experience is designed to integrate knowledge and skills of the core MPH and concentration competencies by applying these skills and knowledge to address relevant public health problems. Students also discuss and reflect on their own growth as public health professionals.

title: Professional Paper
subject: Public Health
description: The professional paper allows the student to engage in analyzing or solving a real public health problem. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Public Health Practicum
subject: Public Health
description:
Individually arranged field experience to develop and refine professional public health skills. Offered on a CR/NC basis only. 
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Public Health
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Special Topics in Advanced Epidemiology
subject: Public Health
description: Special topics in advanced epidemiology for doctoral students in the Epidemiology Concentration.

title: Social Epidemiology Public Health
subject: Public Health
description: In this course we will explore epidemiological methods through the lens of social epidemiology. For the purposes of this course “social epidemiology” will be defined as the use of epidemiological methods to understand the relationship between the social determinants of health and health outcomes. I have structured the course so that for the beginning part of the course we explore a different topic area in social epidemiology week by week, followed by a discussion of interventions and study designs toward the end of the course. This course is not comprehensive of all social determinants and is meant to be an introduction to the field of social epidemiology.

title: Biostatistics Interdisciplinary Capstone Course
subject: Public Health
description: Students will be trained to members of a multi-disciplinary research team and generate study designs including statistical power calculation and analysis plans for research grant proposals; conduct analysis, and communicate results for dissemination.

title: Critical Methodologies and Social Justice Interventions
subject: Public Health
description: This course is designed to challenge the student to examine the correlation between the values of social justice, the literature on the social determinants of health (or causes of the causes, i.e. the environment in which a person lives, works, & plays), health equity and poor health outcomes, focusing on New Mexico. The course will explore the intersectionality of culture, race, class, gender, education, and other forms of identity, from a socio-political context, with implications for policy, practices, and programs that can transform socio-environmental conditions towards health.

title: Culture, Meaning and Power in Health Equity
subject: Public Health
description: In one of his seminal essays on culture, the anthropologist Clifford Geertz underlined the conviction that there is virtually no part of human life that is not shaped by culture. He wrote, “what man [sic] is may be so entangled with where he is, who he is, and what he believes that it is inseparable from them.” Yet, much contemporary research—including the science of health equity—still largely reduces culture to a basic set of characteristics to be controlled for or adapted to. This course will draw on perspectives across disciplines, including philosophy, anthropology, sociology, and community psychology, to explore how culture and power shape the health of individuals and populations, as well as our efforts to achieve health equity.

title: Theory-Based Intervention Research
subject: Public Health
description: Theory plays a pivotal role in the research process, serving as a foundation for justifying the selection of a topic and the development of research questions, design approaches, and analysis plans. Social and behavioral science theories have been instrumental in advancing public health research and practice. This course is designed for graduate students and investigators planning to conduct population or clinical research within a public health approach, offering a comprehensive overview of fundamental conceptual and methodological considerations through a health equity lens.

title: Introduction to Qualitative Methods
subject: Public Health
description: PH 654 is a course created for the COPH PhD in Health Equity Sciences program and focused on qualitative research and dissemination for health equity.  This course will introduce and explore qualitative methods including the major traditions, principles, and methods of qualitative inquiry. The focus of this course will provide PhD students with an opportunity to apply qualitative research design and knowledge development to assignments and develop critical skills to critique peer-reviewed qualitative research publications through a public health and health equity lens.

title: Community Based Participatory Research Lab
subject: Public Health
description: Provides Community Based Participatory Research doctoral concentration students with a mentored research lab to apply their understandings of community engaged and participatory theories, principles, design and methods in a concentration or community engaged research project.

title: Doctoral Special Topics
subject: Public Health
description: This is a special topics course created for the PhD in Health Equity Sciences.

title: Global Health Systems and Policies
subject: Public Health
description:
This course provides an overview of the core topics on global health, including global conditions, policies that shaped the
field, governance and cooperation systems, and the complex itinerary of the health systems during globalization.

title: Advanced Health Policy Analysis
subject: Public Health
description: This course discusses and explores theoretically driven methods in applied policy analysis through equity and social justice lens. Students will learn the application of five-steps in policy analysis from the approach of evidence informed policy making.

subject: Philosophy

A survey of main themes in Dilthey, Husserl, Scheler, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Sartre, Hermeneutics, Structuralism, Deconstruction and the Frankfurt School.  
Prerequisite: one course in Philosophy.

subject: Philosophy
description: This course is a survey of the main epistemological, ontological and conceptual issues that arise from or concern the methodology and content of the empirical sciences.

An examination of the nature and possibility of knowledge. Topics include skepticism, the analysis of knowledge, and the nature and structure of epistemic justification.
Prerequisite: 2210.

title: Metaphysics
subject: Philosophy
description:
Problems and theories of metaphysics. Topics may include: investigation into the structure of things and their properties, identity and individuation, causation, necessity and possibility, universals, mind and body, space and time, God, truth and naturalism. 
Prerequisite: one course in Philosophy.

title: Symbolic Logic
subject: Philosophy
description: This is a first course in logical theory. Its primary goal is to study the notion of logical entailment and related concepts, such as consistency and contingency. Formal systems are developed to analyze these notions rigorously.

title: Ethical Theory
subject: Philosophy
description:
Inquiry concerning goodness, rightness, obligation, justice and freedom. 
Prerequisite: one course in Philosophy.

title: Modern Christian Thought
subject: Philosophy
description:

Prerequisite: one course in Philosophy or Religious Studies.

subject: Philosophy

subject: Philosophy

description: This course focuses on some of the ethical issues that arise in the context of professional life. title: Political Ideas: Introduction to Political Theory
subject: Political Science
description: This course offers an introductory survey of political theory. Emphasis is placed on (1) textual analysis of primary sources and on (2) scholarly analysis of the foundational questions and methods central to the academic study of political ideas. Studying political ideas involves thinking about a) the very definition of political theory itself, b) what one would need to know in order to make evidence- based claims about political theory texts and c) why and how the study of political theory leads political scientists into the exploration of “essentially contested concepts.” More specifically, throughout the semester, we will explore questions relating to 1) what is the definition of political theory; 2) why/how are interpretative disputes at the core of political theory and 3) how have major political theories/ideas—democracy, liberalism, conservatism, socialism, liberation theory, and fascism—changed and developed over time? In sum, this is a survey course on the history of political ideas.

title: Introduction to Political Analysis
subject: Political Science
description: What makes the field of political science a science? What are the variety of research methods and tools for analysis employed by scholars? The goal of this course is to introduce students to the scientific process by political scientists. The interpretation and analysis of data is also essential for almost any career that a political science major might pursue. Lawyers and lobbyists, politicians and professors all need to be able to read and understand reports in which numerical summaries of data (i.e., statistics) are used as evidence to support an argument or point of view. These professionals need to ascertain whether these statistics are being used appropriately. In addition, many of these professionals need to do their own statistical analysis. This course introduces students to statistics and the scientific study of politics. Students will learn why statistics are useful, how to interpret a variety of statistics, how to analyze data to generate their own statistics, and how to tell whether their statistics support their own argument. Students will also learn how to apply the scientific research process to their own research questions by completing a research design project.

title: Public Policy and Administration
subject: Political Science
description: The objective of this introductory course in public policy and public administration is to provide students with a basic understanding of the ways that government deals with problems affecting society. We will explore the political tools used to address public policy problems, as well as the political environment in which public policies are formed. Additionally, several specific public policy problems will be discussed during the semester. For each topic, we will try to understand the goals that the government and society seem to be seeking, alternative means for achieving those goals, the costs and benefits of the various alternatives, and the impact of politics on those goals. We will primarily examine policymaking at the national level, but we will also look at some examples at the state and local level.

introduce students to basic neuromuscular and biomechanical principles of human movement. Muscle origin, insertion and
actions will also be covered.

homeschool children the last six weeks of the course.

professional physical education teacher and to develop the beginning skill set of a high-quality educator. The teacher
candidates will be given the opportunity to observe professional physical education teachers in their classrooms, from

Review of the historical, scientific and ethical issues in the field of psychopathology. Categorization of deviant behavior, theories of abnormal behavior, systems of therapy and relevant research are covered. 
Prerequisite: PSYC 1110.

Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Clinical Psychology Laboratory

It will teach students how to read and critique the relevant literature in an area and how to design solid studies to answer specific research questions. 
Prerequisite: 2510 and 332.

subject: Psychology

title: Human Neuropsychology
subject: Psychology
description:

Prerequisite: PSYC 2250.

title: Neuroscience of Aging and Dementia

General survey of topics in the cognitive and brain sciences of aging and dementia. Topics include the etiology of dementia subtypes, treatment, management, and the socioeconomic impact of an increasingly older population demographic.
Prerequisite: 2250.

This is an advanced psychology course designed for those with an interest in the field of forensic psychology. Forensic psychology applies psychological art and science to legal and quasi-legal problems.

Prerequisite: PSYC 2220 or PSYC 2270.

title: Psychology of Perception
subject: Psychology

Study of the methods organisms use to gain information about objects. The sensory processes are discussed as a basis for description of more complex perceptual phenomena.  
Prerequisite: PSYC 2220 or PSYC 2270.

title: Psychology of Language
subject: Psychology

title: The Psychology of Horror
subject: Psychology

This course explores the emotion of horror both from the standpoint of theoretical and empirical work on emotion and from the standpoint of critical approaches to the phenomenon of horror in art. 
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Cultural Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: Impact of culture on human behavior, learning, personality and other selected topics is examined. Course emphasizes critical analysis, discussion and writing about cross-cultural research and theory.

title: Psychology of Gender
subject: Psychology

Survey of research and theory on gender-role stereotypes and gender differences in such contexts as interpersonal relations, the family, the work force, mass media, mental and physical health.
Prerequisite: PSYC 1110.

Prerequisite: 332.

This seminar examines research on prevention, diagnosis and treatment of clinical depressions and mania. 

Prerequisites: 2250 and 332.

Prerequisite: 2120 and 332.

Students read original research reports and discuss research methods. Background in neuroscience and mathematics necessary. 
Prerequisite: 302 and 2250.

The course reviews the psychological science of emotion, particularly the application of objective physiological and neural measurements. Topics will include historical perspective, neuroscience of emotion, physiology of stress, disorders of emotion, and more. 
Prerequisite: PSYC 1110.

subject: Psychology
description: Continuation of 491. Three hrs. lab.

Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

title: Psychological Research with Diverse Populations
subject: Psychology
description: This course introduces students to various structural factors that may be challenging for different populations, and different research methods and approaches to engaging and working with diverse populations in culturally appropriate and effective manners.

title: Advanced Health Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: This course will examine research and theory on important issues in health psychology including stress, health behaviors, and managing chronic disease. Learning tools include analyzing, synthesizing, and integrating readings and discussing them in class.

title: Health Psychology Interventions
subject: Psychology
description: This course will examine research and theory on application of psychological interventions to health problems including coping with illness and health behavior change.  The interventions will include stress management, mediation, and cognitive behavior therapies.

title: Health Disparities
subject: Psychology
description:
This course introduces students to various significant factors that affect health outcomes for a population differently that the general US population, and culturally appropriate research approaches in working with diverse populations experiencing a disparity.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Seminar on Cognitive Development
subject: Psychology
description: A seminar covering theory and research on the development of cognition, organized around Piaget's constructivist model of cognitive development and subsequent challenges, both theoretical and empirical, to that model.

title: Pre-Clinical Practicum
subject: Psychology
description: This is a core course required for doctoral students in clinical psychology.  The purpose of this course is to introduce you to concepts and basic skills that will prepare you for practicum experiences.  It is intended as a general introduction to concepts, practices and skills that are common to all methods of psychotherapy, and will be complimentary to the individual and group supervision you will be receiving.

title: Seminar in Psychopathology
subject: Psychology
description:
A research-bases course that provides a comprehensive study of abnormal behavior. It stresses diagnosis and assessment of psychopathology and examines various theories of etiology. Recommended treatments are mentioned briefly.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Psychological Evaluation: Cognitive and Neuropsychology Functions
subject: Psychology
description: Provides an introduction to intelligence testing, contemporary factors influencing intellectual performance, and clinical interpretation of cognitive tests. The neuropsychological implications of cognitive deficits are reviewed, along with different approaches to neuropsychological assessment.

title: Psychological Evaluation: Personality Functions
subject: Psychology
description: This course examines: 1) psychometric principles involved in the development and evaluation of psychological tests; 2) major means of personality inventory construction; and 3) the general logic of major personality assessment procedures, including MMPI and Rorschach.

title: Introduction to Clinical Science
subject: Psychology
description:
This course is intended to serve as an introduction to the issues and literature concerned with the science of clinical psychology.
Restriction: admitted to Ph.D. Psychology.

title: Child Psychopathology
subject: Psychology
description: Theories and practices related to an understanding of children and adolescents who deviate from normal development either intellectually, educationally, emotionally, physically or in some combination. Relevant family variables are considered.

title: Biological Bases of Behavior
subject: Psychology
description: Provides an introduction to basic aspects of neuroscience; e.g., historical perspectives, neurocytology, neurophysiology, neurochemistry, neuropharmacology, neuroanatomy. In depth critical discussion of fundamental and current topics.

title: Introduction to Functional Neuroimaging
subject: Psychology
description:
Provides an introduction to functional neuroimaging, from its history to the present. Technical aspects of commonly used neuroimaging methods will be discussed, along with their interpretation and application to questions in psychology and medicine. 
Restriction: Psychology graduate students only.

title: Seminar in Recovery of Function and Epilepsy
subject: Psychology
description: Focuses on the literature and current experiments on epilepsy and functional recovery, the two major problems following traumatic brain injury or stroke. Mechanisms of these processes and clinical advancements will be discussed.

title: Functional Neuroanatomy
subject: Psychology
description: The basics of human neuroanatomy and brain networks are described based on data recorded by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), positron emission tomography PET, electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG) and transcranial stimulation

title: Graduate Problems
subject: Psychology
description: Individual research into an area proposed by the student and conducted under the direction of a faculty member.

title: Cognitive Processes I
subject: Psychology
description: Surveys the major topics and issues in lower order cognitive processes. Includes coverage of fundamental theoretical and empirical work in sensory detection, attention, perception, and motor control.

title: Seminar in Thought and Language
subject: Psychology
description: The role of language in human cognition is approached from a sociocultural framework. Topics: semiotic systems, languages of the mind, categorization, problem solving, and cognitive pluralism.

title: Seminar in Psycholinguistics
subject: Psychology
description: Course emphasizes investigation, evaluation, and discussion of areas of specialized knowledge or inquiry relevant to the profession or field of study.

title: Master's Thesis
subject: Psychology
description:
Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a master’s thesis.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Multivariate Statistics
subject: Psychology
description: Course provides overview of multivariate (MV) methods often used in psychology: data screening; multiple regression, MANOVA, MANCOVA, discriminant analysis, exploratory factor analysis, multiway frequency logistic models; brief introductions to structural equation models and multi-level models. Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Advanced Latent Variable Modeling
subject: Psychology
description: The goal of this course is to cover a range of latent variable models that can be used to characterize unobserved variables, including factor analysis, factor mixture modeling, and latent growth and growth mixture models.

title: Case Conference Practicum
subject: Psychology
description: A bimonthly seminar learning experience where clinical graduate students meet with faculty to present and discuss ongoing, interesting or challenging cases. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Culture and Human Development
subject: Psychology
description: This course introduces students to concept and method in cultural psychology and developmental science, focusing on how development proceeds within a variety of cultural contexts and at various levels of psychological functioning.

title: Seminar in Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy
subject: Psychology
description: Course emphasizes investigation, evaluation, and discussion of areas of specialized knowledge or inquiry relevant to the profession or field of study.

title: Psychotherapy Practicum I
subject: Psychology
description:
Graduate students in the doctoral program in clinical psychology provide psychotherapy to clients in the UNM Psychology Clinic under the supervision of the clinical faculty.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Ethics and Professional Issues in Clinical Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: This seminar is principally concerned with ethics in psychology research, service delivery, training and teaching. Topics in career development and contemporary controversies in professional psychology are also dealt with.

title: Diversity Multicultural Perspectives in Clinical Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
This course provides an overview of multicultural counseling including the principles of understanding one's values and biases, understanding and respecting the client's worldview, and using culturally appropriate interventions.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Empirically Supported Treatments
subject: Psychology
description: The purpose of the seminar is to provide a broad overview of the empirically-supported treatments movement and to teach student how to effectively deliver empirically-supported treatments for specific psychological disorders.

title: Seminar in Cognition, Brain and Behavior
subject: Psychology
description: Critical examination of recent empirical and theoretical articles on behavioral/cognitive neuroscience topics selected by students.

title: Psychobiology of Emotion
subject: Psychology
description: The course reviews the psychological science of emotion, particularly the application of objective physiological and neural measurements. Topics will include historical perspective, neuroscience of emotion, physiology of stress, disorders of emotion, and more.

title: Advanced EEG Analysis in MatLab
subject: Psychology
description: The goal of the course is to provide a conceptual, mathematical, and pragmatic understanding of neural time series data, especially in regard to electroencephalographic (EEG) signals.

title: Special Topics in Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: Study of any psychological topic not otherwise included in the curriculum upon expression of mutual interest by students and faculty.

title: Clinical Internship
subject: Psychology
description: Available only to students who have successfully completed their dissertations. This is a one-year, full-time external clinical internship in which students provide treatment, assessment, and other relevant professional services under intensive and direct professional supervision.

title: Dissertation
subject: Psychology
description: Faculty-supervised investigative study that results in the development and writing of a doctoral dissertation. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.

title: Introduction to Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: This course will introduce students to the concepts, theories, significant findings, methodologies, and terminology that apply to the field of psychology.

title: Social Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
This course is an introduction to the scientific study of human social influence and interaction, and explores how an individual’s actions, emotions, attitudes and thought processes are influenced by society and other individuals.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Developmental Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
Study of human physical and psychological change and stability from a lifespan development perspective.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Cognitive Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
The course provides an overview of human cognitive processes such as attention, perception, memory, language, categorization, decision-making, reasoning, and problem solving. Includes methods, theories, and applications.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Applied Psychology
subject: Psychology
description: Explanation of the psychological principles of everyday living. Emphasizes motivation, learning of intelligent behavior, and applications of psychology to social issues.

title: Brain and Behavior
subject: Psychology
description:
A general survey of the biological foundations of behavior and mental processes. Students will gain an understanding of anatomy, physiology, and chemistry of the nervous system and their relationships to human behavior.
Prerequisite: 1110 or BIOL 1110 or BIOL 1140.

title: Psychology of Learning and Memory
subject: Psychology
description:
This course provides an overview of how information is acquired, stored, retrieved, and manifested in the behavior of human and non-human animals.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Health Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
This course examines how biological, psychological, and social factors interact with and affect different areas within health. Course will cover the role of stress in illness, coping with illness, pain management, and the role of health behavior in health and disease.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
subject: Psychology
description:
Exploration of the psychological, physiological, cultural, social and individual factors that influence sexual behavior, sex roles, and sex identity.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Statistical Principles for Psychology
subject: Psychology
description:
This course covers introductory-level topics in statistics that are applicable to psychological research. Both descriptive and inferential statistics are covered. Topics include applying statistical formulas to psychological data and interpreting the results of statistical analyses.
Prerequisite: 1110.

title: Foundations
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course addresses foundations for patient care that will be further developed in subsequent courses. Content includes principles of exercise physiology, documentation, professionalism, ethics, kinesiology, pathology, pharmacology, imaging, learning styles, mind/body, and therapeutic interventions.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Musculoskeletal Intervention I
subject: Physical Therapy
description: Orthopaedic physical therapy treatment techniques including exercise based treatments, soft tissue techniques and physical agents including electrical, electromagnetic, mechanical modalities.

title: Musculoskeletal Concepts and Management I
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Philosophy, process and techniques of patient examination and evaluation, including patient interview, systems review, differential diagnosis and neuromusculoskeletal assessment. Therapeutic interventions, including modalities, orthotics, manual therapy, and therapeutic exercise will be addressed.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Musculoskeletal Concepts and Management II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course introduces orthopedic physical therapy of ankle, foot, cervical spine, TMJ, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand, and serves as a foundation course for the remainder of the curriculum.  The course will enable the student to interview and evaluate a patient.

title: Musculoskeletal Intervention II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course addresses foundations for orthopedic treatment including exercise and physical agents. This class is designed around regional anatomy and follows both the anatomy and orthopedic evaluation courses.

title: Clinical Education Experience I
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Nine-week clinical education experience provides opportunity to participate in screening, systems review, examination, evaluation, formulation, implementation/modification of plan of care, discharge procedures, scheduling, coordination of patient care activities, supervision of support personnel, documentation for patients/clients.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Professional Patient Management in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: The purpose of this course is to gain practice with effective communication techniques prior to the first clinical education experience. This course involves large and small group discussion and collaboration to develop professional behaviors.  Case-based learning is used to analyze problems that may occur within various PT relationships, with a focus on maintaining curiosity and objectivity to strategize and develop solutions.  This course will also orient students to the objectives and expectations of the first full-time clinical education experience.

title: Management of Integumentary Dysfunction
subject: Physical Therapy
description: Introduce the student to the structure and function of the integumentary system, in order to understand the implications of integumentary dysfunction and/or assess risk of injury to the integumentary function. Restriction: Admitted to DPT Physical Therapy.

title: Human Anatomy I
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will involve dissection and study of the human body.  Lecture material will highlight the nervous system; osteology of the lower extremity, and spinal column; the vascular system and the muscular system of the lower extremities, abdomen, neck, and back; the physiology of the cavities (cardiac, pleural and peritoneal).

title: Human Anatomy II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will involve dissection and study of the human body.  Lecture material will highlight the nervous system including the cranial nerves; osteology of the upper extremity, cranium, spinal column; the vascular system and the muscular system of the upper extremities, head and neck.

title: Evidenced Based Physical Therapy I
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will teach the principles of evidence based physical therapy practice in patient/client management from the initial clinical question to the analysis of the targeted research.  The course will teach the student how to recognize quality in research, increasing the student’s understanding of and confidence in their interpretation of the research.  Students will learn how to critically appraise research, how to find answers to specific foreground questions, and how to interpret statistical data presented within all types of research. Initiation of “mini capstone” process that will complete in EBPT2.

title: Pharmacology for Physical Therapists
subject: Physical Therapy
description: It is essential that a physical therapist be able to make appropriate treatment versus referral decisions with each patient evaluation because of increased responsibility in health management. A component of that is evaluation of the medications your patient is taking, consideration of whether medication side effects may contribute to the symptoms you observe and knowledge of side effects that impact rehabilitation treatments. Therefore, pharmacological treatment and mediation side effects will be addressed, including potential interactions between pharmacological agents and physical therapy practice. Medications will be discussed congruent with the respective physiological system.

title: Pathophysiology
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Study of the pathophysiology, clinical presentation and implications to physical therapy practice of common disease entities that affect the human body.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Prosthetics in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: The purpose for this course is to develop students’ clinical skills for caring patients with limb loss. The class emphasizes biomechanical concepts for pre- and post-prosthetic trainings as a part of the interdisciplinary approach for rehabilitation after amputations.

title: Management of Neurologic Dysfunction IV
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Students learn cognitive, observational, psychomotor skills necessary to examine, manage patients with neurologic dysfunction with an emphasis on adults with spinal cord injury, stroke, traumatic brain injury.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Management of Neurologic Dysfunction II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course applies the concepts of neuroscience and neuropathology and illustrates the correlations with clinical practice.  The student will learn cognitive, observational, and psychomotor skills necessary to examine and manage adults with neurologic dysfunction with an emphasis on patients with stroke, Parkinson’s disease, and cerebellar dysfunction.

title: Management of Neurologic Dysfunction III
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Enhances content from 606L and 609L. Students learn cognitive, observational, psychomotor skills necessary to examine, manage patients with neurologic dysfunction with an emphasis on adults with spinal cord injury, stroke, traumatic brain injury. 
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Management of Neurologic Dysfunction I
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course introduces the student to neuroanatomy and neuropathology and illustrate the correlations to clinical practice. The student will learn cognitive, observational and psychomotor skills necessary to assess and manage adults with neurologic dysfunction. Principles of neurologic examination and evaluation, including neurologic tests and outcome measures, will be introduced.  Case studies will be presented throughout the course to highlight these clinical scenarios

title: Acute Care
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course is designed to enable students to practice in an acute/critical care setting. Topics include cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and general acute care, including ICU equipment, lab values, pharmacology, evaluation, treatment and discarge planning.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Clinical Education Experience II
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Nine-week clinical education experience provides opportunity to participate in screening, systems review, examination, evaluation, formulation, implementation/modification of plan of care, discharge procedures, scheduling, coordination of patient care activities, supervision of support personnel, documentation for patients/clients.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Physical Therapy I
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course gives an overview of normal cardiovascular and pulmonary function, pathologies, examination and evaluation, and differential diagnosis. Labs will focus on developing cardiovascular and pulmonary related assessment techniques in order to perform a cardiovascular and pulmonary oriented patient examination. Successful completion of this course requires the ability to integrate and synthesize information from this course across multiple cardiac, pulmonary, and vascular diagnoses.

title: Biopsychosocial Practice
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
The purpose of this course is to develop the student's awareness of psychosocial and cultural issues of the health professional and the patient, necessary to provide optimal care to patients. Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Specialty Topics in Neurologic Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will look at specialty neurological physical therapy topics primarily focused on the vestibular system including extension into concussion management and EMG studies and interpretation.  The student will be working towards independent evaluation of patients with specialty diagnosis including vestibular diagnoses and post-concussion syndrome from a position driven evaluation with gestalt reasoning to determine the relevant areas of the evaluation that must be completed based on the history and what presents through the evaluation.  The emphasis of the course will be on diagnostic evaluation and treatment of specialty neurological topics.  Evaluation will include diagnoses including both central and peripheral vestibular disorders, post-concussion syndrome, and EMG studies along with the various evidence based treatments associated with these diagnoses.  As a clinical class, much time will be spent on problem solving real life clinical problems by using volunteer patients both from the class and from people associated with the class.

title: Special Topics in Biomechanics, Gait and Movement Analysis in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will introduce fundamental biomechanics utilized in physical therapy practice. The primary emphasis is to obtain clinical decision-making skills to evaluate human movements related to the mechanical properties of motion at a joint, as well as forces and muscle actions. This course will provide students various lab activities utilizing a 3D motion capture system and other assessment tools (e.g., force platforms, pressure mapping and electromyography) as well as low-cost motion capture options.

title: Evidence Based Physical Therapy II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: The primary emphasis of Evidence-based Physical Therapy is to provide the student with skills to become critical consumers of the rehabilitation literature and inform their clinical practice. EBPT2 builds on EBPT1 and expands the critical analysis process to various types of study designs. Students will review current published physical therapy studies and discuss strengths and risk of bias as it pertains to applying the study findings to PT practice. Students will learn how to calculate and interpret common statistics in physical therapy and epidemiological research.  The “mini-capstone” continues in EPBT2 with emphasis on synthesizing the information from the critical appraisal worksheets to write an informed discussion and clinical bottom line. Concepts learned in EBPT will be a cornerstone to understanding other research as students advance in the program.

title: Gender Health
subject: Physical Therapy
description: The purpose of this course is to enhance the students’ knowledge of physical therapy evaluation, goal setting and treatments related to the following conditions: pelvic health/pelvic floor dysfunction (e.g. incontinence, pelvic pain, pelvic organ prolapse, prostate health); bowel, bladder and sexual function in the patient with neurologic dysfunction; perinatal health (e.g. pregnancy, intrapartum & postpartum care); transgender and sexual health; intimate partner violence and strategies for working with survivors of abuse.

title: Clinical Spanish in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: There are an ever-increasing number of people in the U.S. who only speak Spanish, and this trend is reflected in the patient population.  This course goes over health disparities related to language disconcordant care and best practices for working with a medical interpreter. This course will offer an overview of basic anatomy, basic medical vocabulary, grammar and conversation with an emphasis on verb tenses most necessary for communication with Spanish speaking patients.  Grammar will include verb conjugation into the imperative and present tense.  The expectation is not for students to develop Spanish fluency, but rather a basis of language skills that allows the student to communicate in accordance with their skill level, and as appropriate with the help of an interpreter. Students will develop an understanding how to safely work with patients who have limited English proficiency.

title: Pain and Differential Diagnosis in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will address key reasoning process that underlie effective differential diagnosis. This course will build on examination and evaluations skills and integrate this with knowledge of pathology and pathogenesis in clinical populations. In this course you will learn to effectively screen patients for appropriateness of care (in an outpatient PT setting) and what referral and documentation steps must be taken if a patient is deemed inappropriate. Additionally, this course will also provide a basic overview of pain science, assessment and treatment of complex pain conditions.

title: Clinical Education Experience III
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Nine-week clinical education experience provides opportunity to participate in screening, systems review, examination, evaluation, formulation, implementation/modification of plan of care, discharge procedures, scheduling, coordination of patient care activities, supervision of support personnel, documentation for patients/clients.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Core Values in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: The purpose of this course is for learners to actively engage with the nine core values for the Physical Therapist as defined by the APTA: accountability, altruism, collaboration, compassion/caring, duty, excellence, inclusion, integrity, and social responsibility (see appendix for full document). This will be accomplished through service-learning and IPE experiences and active participation in scheduled seminars throughout the 3-year program.

title: Clinical Education Experience IV
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
Ten-week clinical education experience provides opportunity to participate in screening, systems review, examination, evaluation, formulation, implementation/modification of plan of care, discharge procedures, scheduling, coordination of patient care activities, supervision of support personnel, documentation for patients/clients.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Physical Therapy II
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course educates students on cardiovascular and pulmonary interventions based off of pre-requisitive examination and evaluation skills learned in PT613. Labs will focus on performing, modification, and identification the appropriate patient to make use of cardiopulmonary and vascular interventions. Labs will focus on hands-on cardiopulmonary and vascular skills necessary for the entry level physical therapist, including the conduction of a patient treatment session. Successful completion of this course requires the ability to apply and adapt cardiovascular and pulmonary intervention principles across multiple cardiac, pulmonary, and vascular diagnoses.

title: Health, Wellness, and Fitness
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will maximize the student’s understanding of health, wellness and fitness as it relates to their future clients and patients.  Students will also gain an in-depth understanding of the various issues in health promotion from a physical therapy perspective.

title: Pediatrics in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course focuses on application of current models of physical therapy assessment and intervention for typically developing children and children with various conditions that affect normal growth and development during infancy, childhood and adolescence.

title: Gerontology
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
In-depth study of evaluation and clinical management of the geriatric patient/client across the continuum of care.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Administration and Supervision
subject: Physical Therapy
description: This course will prepare students to practice in an increasingly complex health care delivery system. Emphasis includes personnel supervision, practice regulatory and legal requirement issues, reimbursement, litigation, and ethics related to service delivery.

title: Advanced Musculoskeletal Concepts
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course will look at orthopaedic physical therapy of primarily the spine, with extension to the upper and lower extremity. The student will be exposed to the history of, theories behind and a limited scope of the skill of dry needling. The emphasis of the course will be on diagnostic evaluation and treatment using multiple approaches (Nordic, Cyriax, Australian, Paris, Greenman, Functional mobilization, Maitland). Treatment techniques covered will include an introduction to functional dry needling, mobilization, muscle energy and thrust, as well as therapeutic exercise as it relates to mechanical spinal, upper quarter, and lower quarter pain. As a clinical class, much time will be spent on problem solving real life clinical problems by using volunteer patients. 
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Capstone Project
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course is the academic home for a comprehensive evidence-based practice project that definitvely, and in a completely supported manner, answers a focused clinical question. A comprehensive paper and platform presentation are required.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Board Preparation
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
An intensive overview of test-taking and study strategies and review of all major content areas in the National Physical Therapy Exam.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Integrated Clinical Experiences
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course is conducted at REACH clinic, a laboratory clinical setting, with a faculty mentor. Students give short presentations summarizing the presentation of their patients, the chosen interventions, and the plan of care and goals.
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Physical Therapy Independent Study
subject: Physical Therapy
description:
This course is a supervised independent study for students to complete an elective academic experience of relevance to physical therapy or to complete a course required for graduation, such as a clinical internship.
Restriction: admitted to D.P.T. Physical Therapy.

title: Special Topics in Physical Therapy
subject: Physical Therapy
description: Content varies, students may be registered for several sections concurrently.

title: The Craft of Policy Analysis
subject: Public Policy
description: This course bridges the academic - policy worlds by training students in systematic policy analysis that considers historical and community context, evaluates the evidence base, and explores innovative approaches.

title: Policy and Evaluation Lab
subject: Public Policy
description:
Experiential learning in policy analysis and program evaluation for government, research, and community organizations. 
Offered on a CR/NC basis only.
Restricion: admitted to M.P.P. Public Policy.

title: Patient Care
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
This course acquaints the student with nursing procedures and techniques emphasizing the role of the diagnostic imager as a member of the healthcare team.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Patient Care Lab
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
This course covers the laboratory activities associated with 330.
Restriction: permission of instructor.

title: Healthcare Delivery and Compliance
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Students are introduced to the history and current trends of the American Healthcare system. Course material will reflect the current healthcare system and the effect the roles have on improving the system.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Medical Language Systems Review
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
This self-study course reviews the major systems of the human body, using a programmed textbook/workbook. The workbook format is combined with simple, non-technical explanations of medical terms and descriptions of anatomy, physiology, and pathology.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Topics in Healthcare Ethics and Diversity
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Students will participate in discussion and reflection on current and landmark healthcare cases. Course activities are designed to allow students to examine and explore ethical issues in the medical field.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Introduction to Research and Medical Imaging
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
The course will focus on the development of a Healthcare research question, completion of an annotated bibliography and a final literature review. This includes exercises in formatting, paraphrasing and avoiding plagiarism.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Community Engagement and Service Learning
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
The course offers students the opportunity to engage in community service and field experience. Students are exposed to the theories and practices of community service, information literacy, patient care, team building and leadership activities. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences and permission of instructor.

title: UNM Radiologic Sciences Independent Study course
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description: This course is designed to provide students with a versatile educational experience in either (BSRS), CT, MRI and or Nuclear Medicine programs. This course offers students the flexibility to emphasize either clinical competency or didactic instruction based on their individual learning preferences and course objectives.

title: Physics of Computed Tomography
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course provides instruction in physics and instrumentation related to computed tomography including the history of the development of computed tomography, system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences or CERT Computed Tomography or CERT Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

title: Physics of Computed Tomography II
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
A continuation of RAD 410 further providing advance instruction in physics and instrumentation related to computed tomography, including the history of the development of computed tomography, system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction.
Prerequisite: 410.  
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Computed Tomography Physics Review
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Comprehensive examinations and topic review will take place throughout the semester. The registry review examinations will encompass the listed topics for students to demonstratre a basic knowledge of computed tomography and physics.
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Computed Tomography Clinical I
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course provides clinical instruction in computed tomography including the system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Computed Tomography Clinical II
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description: Course is a continuation of RADS 420 and provides additional clinical instruction in computed tomography including the system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction.

title: Computed Tomography Clinical III
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course provides additional clinical instruction in computed tomography including the system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction. 
Prerequisite: 420 and 421. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Physics of Magnetic Resonance Imaging I
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course provides additional instruction in physics and instrumentation related to magnetic resonance imaging including the history of the development of magnetic resonance imaging, system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences or CERT Computed Tomography or CERT Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

title: Physics of Magnetic Resonance Imaging II
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course is a continuation of RADS 450. 
Prerequisite: 450. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences or CERT Computed Tomography or CERT Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

title: MRI Physics Review
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Comprehensive examinations and topic review will take place throughout the semester. The registry review examinations will encompass the listed topics for students to demonstrate a basic knowledge of Magnetic Resonance Imaging and physics
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: MRI Clinical I
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course provides clinical instruction in magnetic resonance imaging including system operation and components, image formation and reconstruction, characteristics of image quality, and artifact recognition/reduction. 
Corequisite: 450. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: MRI Clinical II
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course is a continuation of RADS 460. 
Prerequisite: 460. 
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences or CERT Computed Tomography or CERT Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

title: MRI Clinical III
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Practical experience in the performance of magnetic resonance imaging studies under direct supervision of certified technologists and staff radiologists. Includes competency examinations, image evaluation, patient care assessment, imaging protocols, and safety issues.
Prerequisite: 461.  
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

title: Human Cross Sectional Anatomy
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course examines three-dimensional relationships of skull, brain, CNS, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, correlating this information with imaging modalities (CT, MRI, Nuclear Medicine).
Restriction: admitted to B.S. Radiologic Sciences.

This a starred (*) level course and may be taken for graduate credit by students enrolled in a graduate program. A graduate student enrolled in a starred course numbered below 500 may be required to complete extra work.

title: Human Cross Sectional Pathology
subject: Radiologic Sciences
description:
Course examines a basic understanding of the principles of pathology relating to imaging science and the radiographic appearance of specific diseases and processes within the body systems.
Restriction: enrolled in the Radiologic Sciences program.

title: Black Liberation and Religion
subject: Religion
description: Students will be introduced to the Black experience, which necessitates the redefinition of God and Jesus Christ in the lives of Black people as the struggle for transcendental and political freedom.

title: Introduction to Islam
subject: Religion
description: This course examines the life and role of the Prophet Muhammad, the message of the Qur'an, and the history of the theological, philosophical, legal, and mystical dimensions of Islam to the present.

title: Islamic Fundamentalism
subject: Religion
